Review target: `current worktree diff against main; read-only only. Focus on Bash 3.2 correctness; fail-closed exact selectors, JSON/TSV, UUID/path containment/ambiguity; artifact staging plan/no-plan/no-specstory validation and index atomicity; generated hook quoting/global hooksPath; branch/worktree isolation tests; SpecStory 2.10 docs semantics and secret leakage. `max effort → 5+5 angles × 8 candidates → 1-vote verify → sweep → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at maximum effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, 3-state)

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with
the most concrete failure scenario. For each remaining candidate, run **one
verifier** via the Agent tool: give it the diff, the relevant
file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

This is recall mode — a single non-REFUTED vote carries the finding. Do NOT
drop on uncertainty.

## Phase 3 — Sweep for gaps

Run **one more finder** as a fresh reviewer who has the verified list. Re-read
the diff and enclosing functions looking ONLY for defects not already listed.
Do not re-derive or re-confirm anything already there — the job is gaps. Focus
on what the first pass tends to miss: moved/extracted code that dropped a guard
or anchor; second-tier footguns (dataclass default evaluated once, `hash()`
non-determinism, lock-scope shrink, predicate methods with side effects);
setup/teardown asymmetry in tests; config defaults flipped.

Surface **up to 8 additional candidates**, each naming a defect not already on
the list. If nothing new, return an empty sweep — do not pad.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 15 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 15 survive, keep the 15 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

81	 The metadata helper reads staged blobs, not concurrently-changing working
82	 files. It emits deduplicated `AI-Assisted-By: Harness (model)`,
83	 `Agent-Transcript`, and conditional `Agent-Plan` trailers. Pass explicit
84	 `--harness` + `--model` only when a transcript cannot prove that identity.
85	 
86	+`find-session.sh` is exact by default. It anchors at the git root, validates an
87	+exact SpecStory `Claude Code Session UUID` header, and parses the selected raw
88	+Claude JSONL for an exact `sessionId` + `cwd`. TSV and `--json` output include
89	+`status`, `confidence`, `source`, selected paths, and ambiguity candidates.
90	+Missing artifacts, duplicate UUID aliases, and identity mismatches return
91	+nonzero; `--newest` is the only heuristic mode.
92	+
93	+`stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` validates all selectors and paths
94	+before one `git add`. Selector failures exit 5 with the index unchanged. The
95	+no-selector command remains **broad branch-wide compatibility mode** and stages
96	+every dirty Markdown artifact under configured directories; use it only when
97	+that whole set is intentional.

102	+discovery are scoped by **checkout path, not branch**. Switching branches in one
103	+checkout shares the same artifact pool; separate worktrees have separate
104	+`.specstory/history/` roots and Claude project slugs.
105	+
106	+Use **worktree first, wrapper/session second**, with one SpecStory wrapper and
107	+Claude session per change stream. Render a known raw session explicitly with:
108	+
109	+```bash
110	+specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
111	+```
112	+
113	+The same UUID can produce multiple rendered aliases. That is an ambiguity, not
114	+a newest-file tie-break: pass `--specstory-path`. `EnterWorktree` does not
115	+rebind a SpecStory watcher that is already running, so stop it and start a new
116	+wrapper in the target worktree.

230	+## SpecStory 2.10 的 checkout scope
231	+
232	+SpecStory 2.10 的實測行為：rendered output discovery 與 Claude raw session
233	+discovery 都依 **checkout path，而不是 branch** 分隔。同一 checkout 切換 branch
234	+仍共用 artifact pool；不同 worktree 才有不同的 `.specstory/history/` root 與
235	+Claude project slug。
236	+
237	+採用 **先建 worktree，再啟動 wrapper/session** 的順序，每個 change stream 只跑
238	+一組 SpecStory wrapper 與 Claude session。要明確 render 已知的 raw session：
239	+
240	+```bash
241	+specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
242	+```
243	+
244	+同一 UUID 可能產生多個 rendered alias。這是 ambiguity，不應用 newest-file
245	+破除平手；請傳 `--specstory-path`。`EnterWorktree` 不會重新綁定已在運行的
246	+SpecStory watcher，所以要先停止它，再從目標 worktree 啟動新的 wrapper。

466	 ## Available scripts
467	 
468	-- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
469	-  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
470	-  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
471	-  empty fields signal absence).
472	+- **`scripts/find-session.sh (--session-id UUID | --specstory-path PATH | --newest) [--format specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
473	+  Resolve from the git root. Exact mode verifies the SpecStory header plus the
474	+  Claude JSONL filename and parsed `sessionId`/`cwd`; duplicate aliases report
475	+  candidates and exit 4. TSV and JSON both include `status`, `confidence`, and
476	+  `source`. Missing/mismatched identities fail closed; `--newest` is the only
477	+  heuristic path.
478	 
479	-- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
480	-  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
481	-  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
482	-  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.

622	+Claude Code stores raw sessions under:

633	-underscore collapses the same way, which is easy to miss:
634	-`/home/<user>/.local/share/chezmoi` is stored as

1826	 ## Layout
1827	 
1828	 - `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
1829	   Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
1830	   should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
1831	   inside an agent-artifact directory).
1832	 - `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
1833	   `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
1834	 - `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
1835	   redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
1836	   `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
1837	 - `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
1838	   in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
1839	   the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
1840	   not on `PATH`.
1841	 - `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
1842	   `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
1843	   gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.
1844	+- `test_find_session.sh` — exact `sessionId`/`cwd` and SpecStory-header matching,
1845	+  explicit `--newest`, same-checkout branch leakage, duplicate UUID candidates,
1846	+  root-relative paths with spaces, subdirectory calls, and two-worktree isolation.
1847	+- `test_stage_agent_artifacts.sh` — exact plan/no-plan/no-SpecStory policy, one
1848	+  atomic `git add`, unchanged-index selector failures, broad-mode compatibility,
1849	+  exact metadata trailers, and generated hook no-op/error/success behavior.
1850	+- `test_agent_commit_metadata.sh` — staged transcript parsing, model

 Run the full suite:

 ```
 
 ## Layout
 
 - `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
   Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
   should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
   inside an agent-artifact directory).
 - `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
   `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
 - `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
   redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
   `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
 - `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
   in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
   the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
   not on `PATH`.
 - `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
   `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
   gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.
+- `test_find_session.sh` — exact `sessionId`/`cwd` and SpecStory-header matching,
+  explicit `--newest`, same-checkout branch leakage, duplicate UUID candidates,
+  root-relative paths with spaces, subdirectory calls, and two-worktree isolation.
+- `test_stage_agent_artifacts.sh` — exact plan/no-plan/no-SpecStory policy, one
+  atomic `git add`, unchanged-index selector failures, broad-mode compatibility,
+  exact metadata trailers, and generated hook no-op/error/success behavior.
+- `test_agent_commit_metadata.sh` — staged transcript parsing, model
+  deduplication, spaced paths, JSON output, overrides, and bootstrap's global
+  `core.hooksPath` refusal.
 - `test_bootstrap_project.py` — verifies precise, idempotent nested SpecStory
   ignores; confirms `history/` stays visible; checks dry-run and the explicit
   `--untrack-specstory-state` migration contract.
 
 ## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
 
 The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
 `webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
 secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
 `npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:
 
 ```
 <SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->                      # markdown fixtures
 "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n"  # gitleaks:allow  # test_redact_secrets.py
 ```
 
 The Stripe webhook fixture is stricter: GitHub's provider-level scanner does
 not honour gitleaks markers, so its source uses
 `__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__`. The corpus test expands that placeholder
 inside its throwaway repo. The other corpus + shell tests **strip the marker
 before staging** (`_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE` in `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`; the `sed`
 in `stage_fixture` in `test_scan_staged.sh`), so the secret bytes have the exact
 shape the rules expect and the assertions still fire. Principle: **fake test
 vectors are out of scan scope by default, and only "fire" when a test re-plants
 them.**
 
 Invariant — **the strip must be byte-identical**: never change a secret's length
 or the length-sensitive rules (`sk-proj-…{80,}`, `sk-ant-api\d{2}-…{93}AA`, the
 webhook regexes) stop matching. When adding a new firing fixture, append the
 marker with a single leading space (`<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->`); the
 strip regex reclaims exactly that separator. `clean.md` / `example_shapes.md`
 carry no marker (the strip is a no-op) and must keep their must-not-fire
 behavior. GitHub-native secret scanning ignores the marker; it's excluded
 separately via the repo's `.github/secret_scanning.yml`. This replaced a former
 repo-root `.gitleaksignore` whose `file:rule:line` fingerprints silently drifted.

2	# find-session.sh — resolve an exact SpecStory / Claude Code session for a git checkout.
3	#
4	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
5	
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	usage() {
9	  cat <<'EOF'
10	Usage: find-session.sh (--session-id UUID | --specstory-path PATH | --newest) [OPTIONS]
11	
12	Resolve agent session files for the current git checkout. Exact selectors are
13	required unless the caller explicitly opts into the compatibility heuristic.
14	Relative paths are resolved from the git root, not the invocation directory.
15	
16	Selectors:
17	  --session-id UUID       Select the exact Claude Code session UUID. When
18	                          SpecStory output is requested, its header must match.
19	  --specstory-path PATH   Select one exact .specstory/history/*.md file and
20	                          derive/verify its Claude Code session UUID.
21	  --newest                Explicitly use independent newest-file heuristics.
22	                          Cannot be combined with exact selectors.
23	
24	Options:
25	  --format VALUE          specstory, claude, or both (default: both).
26	  --json                  Emit one JSON object instead of TSV.
27	  --quiet                 Suppress stderr diagnostics; structured stdout remains.
28	  --help, -h              Show this help and exit.
29	
30	TSV output keys:
31	  status                  resolved | not_found | ambiguous | mismatch | error
32	  confidence              exact | heuristic | none
33	  source                  session-id | specstory-path | session-id+specstory-path | newest
34	  specstory_path          absolute path or empty
35	  claude_session_uuid     UUID or empty
36	  claude_jsonl_path       absolute path or empty
37	  candidate               repeated absolute candidate path (only when relevant)
38	
39	Exit codes:
40	  0  requested artifacts resolved
41	  1  invalid arguments
42	  2  not inside a git repository
43	  3  requested artifact not found
44	  4  exact selector is ambiguous; candidates are reported
45	  5  selected path/header/JSONL identity failed validation
46	EOF
47	}
48	
49	QUIET=0
50	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
51	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
52	
53	FORMAT="both"
54	OUT_JSON=0
55	SESSION_ID=""
56	SPECSTORY_INPUT=""
57	USE_NEWEST=0
58	
59	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
60	  case "$1" in
61	    --session-id)
62	      shift
63	      [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "--session-id needs a UUID (try --help)" 1
64	      SESSION_ID="$1"; shift ;;
65	    --session-id=*) SESSION_ID="${1#--session-id=}"; shift ;;
66	    --specstory-path)
67	      shift
68	      [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "--specstory-path needs a path (try --help)" 1
69	      SPECSTORY_INPUT="$1"; shift ;;
70	    --specstory-path=*) SPECSTORY_INPUT="${1#--specstory-path=}"; shift ;;
71	    --newest) USE_NEWEST=1; shift ;;
72	    --format)
73	      shift
74	      [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "--format needs specstory, claude, or both (try --help)" 1
75	      FORMAT="$1"; shift ;;
76	    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
77	    --json) OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
78	    --quiet) QUIET=1; shift ;;
79	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
80	    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
81	    *)  die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
82	  esac
83	done
84	
85	case "$FORMAT" in
86	  both|specstory|claude) ;;
87	  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
88	esac
89	
90	if [ "$USE_NEWEST" = "1" ] && { [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] || [ -n "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" ]; }; then
91	  die "--newest cannot be combined with --session-id or --specstory-path" 1
92	fi
93	if [ "$USE_NEWEST" = "0" ] && [ -z "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ -z "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" ]; then
94	  die "exact selection requires --session-id or --specstory-path (use --newest only for the compatibility heuristic)" 1
95	fi
96	if [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$SESSION_ID" | grep -Eq '^[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}$'; then
97	  die "invalid --session-id: expected a canonical UUID, received '$SESSION_ID'" 1
98	fi
99	
100	STATUS="error"
101	CONFIDENCE="none"
102	SOURCE=""
103	SPECSTORY_PATH=""
104	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
105	CLAUDE_UUID="$SESSION_ID"
106	CANDIDATES=()
107	
108	if [ "$USE_NEWEST" = "1" ]; then
109	  SOURCE="newest"
110	elif [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ -n "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" ]; then
111	  SOURCE="session-id+specstory-path"
112	elif [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ]; then
113	  SOURCE="session-id"
114	else
115	  SOURCE="specstory-path"
116	fi
117	
118	json_escape() {
119	  printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'
120	}
121	
122	emit_result() {
123	  local candidate first
124	  if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
125	    printf '{"status":"%s","confidence":"%s","source":"%s"' \
126	      "$(json_escape "$STATUS")" "$(json_escape "$CONFIDENCE")" "$(json_escape "$SOURCE")"
127	    printf ',"specstory_path":"%s"' "$(json_escape "$SPECSTORY_PATH")"
128	    printf ',"claude_session_uuid":"%s"' "$(json_escape "$CLAUDE_UUID")"
129	    printf ',"claude_jsonl_path":"%s","candidates":[' "$(json_escape "$CLAUDE_JSONL")"
130	    first=1
131	    for candidate in "${CANDIDATES[@]:-}"; do
132	      [ -n "$candidate" ] || continue
133	      [ "$first" = "1" ] || printf ','
134	      printf '"%s"' "$(json_escape "$candidate")"
135	      first=0
136	    done
137	    printf ']}\n'
138	  else
139	    printf 'status\t%s\n' "$STATUS"
140	    printf 'confidence\t%s\n' "$CONFIDENCE"
141	    printf 'source\t%s\n' "$SOURCE"
142	    printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
143	    printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
144	    printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
145	    for candidate in "${CANDIDATES[@]:-}"; do
146	      [ -n "$candidate" ] && printf 'candidate\t%s\n' "$candidate"
147	    done
148	  fi
149	  return 0
150	}
151	
152	fail_result() {
153	  STATUS="$1"
154	  CONFIDENCE="none"
155	  local message="$2" rc="$3" candidate
156	  log "error: $message"
157	  if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
158	    log "candidates:"
159	    for candidate in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
160	      log "  $candidate"
161	    done
162	  fi
163	  emit_result
164	  exit "$rc"
165	}
166	
167	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
168	  fail_result "error" "not inside a git repository" 2
169	fi
170	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
171	SPECSTORY_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.specstory/history"
172	
173	case "$REPO_ROOT" in
174	  *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*$'\r'*) fail_result "mismatch" "git root contains an unsupported tab, carriage return, or newline" 5 ;;
175	esac
176	
177	cwd_slug() {
178	  printf '%s' "$REPO_ROOT" | sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9]|-|g'
179	}
180	
181	canonical_existing_file() {
182	  local input="$1" absolute parent base
183	  case "$input" in
184	    /*) absolute="$input" ;;
185	    *)  absolute="$REPO_ROOT/$input" ;;
186	  esac
187	  [ -f "$absolute" ] || return 1
188	  parent="$(cd "$(dirname "$absolute")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || return 1
189	  base="$(basename "$absolute")"
190	  printf '%s/%s' "$parent" "$base"
191	}
192	
193	specstory_header_uuid() {
194	  sed -n -E 's/^<!-- Claude Code Session ([0-9A-Fa-f]{8}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}) \([^)]*\) -->$/\1/p' "$1" \
195	    | head -n 1
196	}
197	
198	validate_specstory_path() {
199	  local path="$1" uuid
200	  case "$path" in
201	    "$SPECSTORY_DIR"/*.md) ;;
202	    *) return 2 ;;
203	  esac
204	  uuid="$(specstory_header_uuid "$path")"
205	  [ -n "$uuid" ] || return 3
206	  printf '%s' "$uuid"
207	}
208	
209	validate_claude_jsonl() {
210	  local path="$1" uuid="$2"
211	  command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 3
212	  python3 - "$path" "$uuid" "$REPO_ROOT" <<'PY'
213	import json
214	import sys
215	
216	path, expected_session, expected_cwd = sys.argv[1:]
217	matched = False
218	saw_identity = False
219	try:
220	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as stream:
221	        for line in stream:
222	            try:
223	                value = json.loads(line)
224	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
225	                # A live writer can leave one incomplete trailing record. Identity
226	                # still has to be proven by another complete JSON object.
227	                continue
228	            if not isinstance(value, dict):
229	                continue
230	            if "sessionId" in value or "cwd" in value:
231	                saw_identity = True
232	            if value.get("sessionId") == expected_session and value.get("cwd") == expected_cwd:
233	                matched = True
234	                break
235	except (OSError, UnicodeError):
236	    sys.exit(2)
237	
238	if matched:
239	    sys.exit(0)
240	sys.exit(1 if saw_identity else 2)
241	PY
242	}
243	
244	newest_file() {
245	  local dir="$1" glob="$2" newest="" file
246	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
247	  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
248	    if [ -z "$newest" ] || [ "$file" -nt "$newest" ]; then
249	      newest="$file"
250	    fi
251	  done < <(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null)
252	  printf '%s' "$newest"
253	}
254	
255	resolve_exact_specstory() {
256	  local selected_uuid="" file uuid
257	  if [ -n "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" ]; then
258	    if ! SPECSTORY_PATH="$(canonical_existing_file "$SPECSTORY_INPUT")"; then
259	      CANDIDATES+=("$SPECSTORY_INPUT")
260	      fail_result "not_found" "SpecStory path does not exist as a file: $SPECSTORY_INPUT" 3
261	    fi
262	    case "$SPECSTORY_PATH" in
263	      *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*$'\r'*)
264	        CANDIDATES+=("$SPECSTORY_PATH")
265	        fail_result "mismatch" "SpecStory path contains an unsupported tab, carriage return, or newline" 5 ;;
266	    esac
267	    CANDIDATES+=("$SPECSTORY_PATH")
268	    if ! selected_uuid="$(validate_specstory_path "$SPECSTORY_PATH")"; then
269	      fail_result "mismatch" "--specstory-path must be a Markdown file directly under the git root's .specstory/history/ with an exact Claude Code Session UUID header" 5
270	    fi
271	    if [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ "$selected_uuid" != "$SESSION_ID" ]; then
272	      fail_result "mismatch" "SpecStory header UUID '$selected_uuid' does not equal --session-id '$SESSION_ID'" 5
273	    fi
274	    CLAUDE_UUID="$selected_uuid"
275	    CANDIDATES=()
276	    return 0
277	  fi
278	
279	  [ -d "$SPECSTORY_DIR" ] || fail_result "not_found" "no .specstory/history directory under git root $REPO_ROOT" 3
280	  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
281	    uuid="$(specstory_header_uuid "$file")"
282	    [ "$uuid" = "$SESSION_ID" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$file")
283	  done < <(find "$SPECSTORY_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null)
284	
285	  case "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" in
286	    0) fail_result "not_found" "no SpecStory transcript has exact Claude Code Session UUID '$SESSION_ID' under $SPECSTORY_DIR" 3 ;;
287	    1) SPECSTORY_PATH="${CANDIDATES[0]}"; CANDIDATES=() ;;
288	    *) fail_result "ambiguous" "multiple SpecStory transcripts have session UUID '$SESSION_ID'; retry with --specstory-path" 4 ;;
289	  esac
290	}
291	
292	resolve_exact_claude() {
293	  local project_dir candidate validation_rc=0
294	  [ -n "$CLAUDE_UUID" ] || fail_result "mismatch" "no Claude session UUID could be derived from the exact selector" 5
295	  project_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(cwd_slug)"
296	  candidate="$project_dir/$CLAUDE_UUID.jsonl"
297	  if [ ! -f "$candidate" ]; then
298	    CANDIDATES+=("$candidate")
299	    fail_result "not_found" "exact Claude JSONL not found for checkout '$REPO_ROOT' and session '$CLAUDE_UUID'" 3
300	  fi
301	  CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
302	  CANDIDATES+=("$candidate")
303	  validate_claude_jsonl "$candidate" "$CLAUDE_UUID" || validation_rc=$?
304	  case "$validation_rc" in
305	    0) CANDIDATES=() ;;
306	    3) fail_result "mismatch" "python3 is required to validate exact Claude JSONL identity" 5 ;;
307	    *) fail_result "mismatch" "Claude JSONL did not contain an exact sessionId/cwd record for '$CLAUDE_UUID' and '$REPO_ROOT'" 5 ;;
308	  esac
309	}
310	
311	resolve_newest() {
312	  local project_dir header_uuid
313	  if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
314	    SPECSTORY_PATH="$(newest_file "$SPECSTORY_DIR" '*.md')"
315	    [ -n "$SPECSTORY_PATH" ] || fail_result "not_found" "no .specstory/history/*.md under git root $REPO_ROOT" 3
316	    header_uuid="$(specstory_header_uuid "$SPECSTORY_PATH")"
317	    [ -n "$header_uuid" ] && CLAUDE_UUID="$header_uuid"
318	  fi
319	  if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
320	    project_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(cwd_slug)"
321	    CLAUDE_JSONL="$(newest_file "$project_dir" '*.jsonl')"
322	    [ -n "$CLAUDE_JSONL" ] || fail_result "not_found" "no Claude JSONL under $project_dir" 3
323	    CLAUDE_UUID="$(basename "$CLAUDE_JSONL" .jsonl)"
324	  fi
325	}
326	
327	if [ "$USE_NEWEST" = "1" ]; then
328	  resolve_newest
329	  STATUS="resolved"
330	  CONFIDENCE="heuristic"
331	else
332	  if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
333	    resolve_exact_specstory
334	  elif [ -n "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" ]; then
335	    # A path can supply the UUID even when only Claude output was requested.
336	    selected_path="$(canonical_existing_file "$SPECSTORY_INPUT" 2>/dev/null || true)"
337	    [ -n "$selected_path" ] || {
338	      CANDIDATES+=("$SPECSTORY_INPUT")
339	      fail_result "not_found" "SpecStory path does not exist as a file: $SPECSTORY_INPUT" 3
340	    }
341	    CANDIDATES+=("$selected_path")
342	    selected_uuid="$(validate_specstory_path "$selected_path" 2>/dev/null || true)"
343	    [ -n "$selected_uuid" ] || fail_result "mismatch" "--specstory-path does not have an exact Claude Code Session UUID header" 5
344	    if [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ "$selected_uuid" != "$SESSION_ID" ]; then
345	      fail_result "mismatch" "SpecStory header UUID '$selected_uuid' does not equal --session-id '$SESSION_ID'" 5
346	    fi
347	    CLAUDE_UUID="$selected_uuid"
348	    CANDIDATES=()
349	  fi
350	  if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
351	    resolve_exact_claude
352	  fi
353	  STATUS="resolved"
354	  CONFIDENCE="exact"
355	fi
356	
357	emit_result
358

233	                matched = True
234	                break
235	except (OSError, UnicodeError):
236	    sys.exit(2)

239	    sys.exit(0)

39	                      chezmoi source ($HOME/.local/share/chezmoi) so updates

52	  --force             Overwrite existing files instead of skipping.
53	  --dry-run           Print what would happen without making changes.
54	  --help, -h          Show this help and exit.

56	Exit codes:
57	  0  success
58	  1  invalid arguments
59	  2  not inside a git repo
60	  3  chezmoi source missing (and --from-chezmoi was requested)
61	  4  pre-commit tool unavailable and `uvx` fallback failed

179	cfg = sys.argv[1]

183	remote_block = (

185	    f"    rev: {rev}\n"
186	    "    hooks:\n"

190	def is_top_item(l):  # a `  - repo:` list entry
191	    return re.match(r"^  - repo:", l) is not None
192

195	    print("already references the pinned hook; nothing to rewrite", file=sys.stderr)

201	        j = i + 1

203	            j += 1

28	                          --session-id so the raw Claude JSONL can still be proved.
29	  --plan PATH             Stage this exact in-repo Markdown plan.
30	  --no-plan               Explicitly state that this session has no plan.

46	  1  invalid arguments
47	  2  not inside a git repository

183	remote_block = (

185	    f"    rev: {rev}\n"

190	def is_top_item(l):  # a `  - repo:` list entry
191	    return re.match(r"^  - repo:", l) is not None

138	  's/^_\*\*(Agent|Assistant) \((.*) [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z\)\*\*_[[:space:]]*$/\2/p')
139	EOF
140	
141	  [ "$found_model" = "1" ] || \
142	    die "could not detect a model from staged transcript: $path (pass --harness and --model)" 4
143	}
144	
145	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
146	  case "$path" in
147	    .specstory/history/*.md) append_unique transcript "$path" ;;
148	    .claude/plans/*.md|.cursor/plans/*.md|.opencode/plans/*.md|.specify/*.md|.codex/*.md)
149	      append_unique plan "$path" ;;
150	  esac
151	done < <(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z)
152	
153	if [ "${#TRANSCRIPTS[@]}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${#PLANS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
154	  die "no staged agent transcript or plan artifacts (stage them first)" 3
155	fi
156	
157	if [ -n "$HARNESS" ]; then
158	  append_unique assistant "$(normalize_harness "$HARNESS") ($MODEL)"
159	else
160	  for transcript in "${TRANSCRIPTS[@]}"; do
161	    parse_transcript "$transcript"
162	  done
163	fi
164	
165	if [ "${#ASSISTANTS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
166	  die "no harness/model provenance resolved (pass --harness and --model)" 4
167	fi
168	
169	json_escape() {
170	  printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'
171	}
172	
173	json_array() {
174	  local kind="$1" first=1 item
175	  printf '['
176	  case "$kind" in
177	    assistant) set -- "${ASSISTANTS[@]}" ;;
178	    transcript) set -- "${TRANSCRIPTS[@]}" ;;
179	    plan) set -- "${PLANS[@]}" ;;
180	  esac
181	  for item in "$@"; do
182	    [ "$first" = "1" ] || printf ','
183	    printf '"%s"' "$(json_escape "$item")"
184	    first=0
185	  done
186	  printf ']'
187	}
188	
189	if [ "$FORMAT" = "json" ]; then
190	  printf '{"assistants":'
191	  json_array assistant
192	  printf ',"transcripts":'
193	  json_array transcript
194	  printf ',"plans":'
195	  json_array plan
196	  printf '}\n'
197	else
198	  for assistant in "${ASSISTANTS[@]}"; do
199	    printf 'AI-Assisted-By: %s\n' "$assistant"
200	  done
201	  for transcript in "${TRANSCRIPTS[@]}"; do
202	    printf 'Agent-Transcript: %s\n' "$transcript"
203	  done
204	  for plan in "${PLANS[@]}"; do
205	    printf 'Agent-Plan: %s\n' "$plan"
206	  done
207	fi
208	
209	log "metadata: ${#ASSISTANTS[@]} assistant(s), ${#TRANSCRIPTS[@]} transcript(s), ${#PLANS[@]} plan(s)"
210

```text
1	# Transcript & session discovery
2	
3	How `find-session.sh` proves that one SpecStory Markdown file and one Claude Code
4	JSONL belong to the same session in the current git checkout.
5	
6	## Exact by default
7	
8	There is no reliable implicit "current session" pointer. Multiple sessions can
9	write under one checkout, and branch switches do not move those files. Therefore
10	`find-session.sh` requires at least one exact selector:
11	
12	```bash
13	# UUID from Claude Code /status
14	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
15	  --session-id 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
16	
17	# Explicit rendered alias; relative paths resolve from the git root
18	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
19	  --specstory-path '.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
20	
21	# Strongest form: both selectors must agree
22	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
23	  --session-id 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab \
24	  --specstory-path '.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
25	```
26	
27	`--newest` is an explicit compatibility heuristic. It independently picks the
28	newest SpecStory Markdown and Claude JSONL by mtime and reports
29	`confidence=heuristic`; it does not prove that the two files belong together.
30	Never use it for exact staging or hooks.
31	
32	## Git-root anchoring
33	
34	The script starts with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and anchors all discovery
35	to that path. Calling it from `src/deep/subdir` is therefore equivalent to
36	calling it from the checkout root. A relative `--specstory-path` is also
37	interpreted from the git root, not the shell's current subdirectory.
38	
39	Paths must be regular Markdown files directly under the checkout's
40	`.specstory/history/`. Outside paths and malformed headers fail closed.
41	
42	## Claude Code session layout and proof
43	
44	Claude Code stores raw sessions under:
45	
46	```
47	~/.claude/projects/<checkout-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl
48	```
49	
50	The slug is the absolute git-root path with **every non-alphanumeric character**
51	replaced by `-`, including dots, underscores, and spaces. For example,
52	`/home/user/.local/project one` becomes
53	`-home-user--local-project-one`. Rebuild it with
54	`sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'`, not `tr '/' '-'`.
55	
56	Exact resolution does not trust the filename alone. It parses complete JSONL
57	records and requires one object whose:
58	
59	- `sessionId` exactly equals the selected UUID; and
60	- `cwd` exactly equals the current git root.
61	
62	A live writer may leave one incomplete trailing JSON line; malformed lines are
63	ignored, but another complete record still has to prove both fields. A correctly
64	named file with another checkout's `cwd` exits as a mismatch.
65	
66	## SpecStory layout, header, and aliases
67	
68	SpecStory writes rendered output under:
69	
70	```
71	<git-root>/.specstory/history/<rendered-name>.md
72	```
73	
74	For Claude sessions, exact matching requires this whole header shape:
75	
76	```markdown
77	<!-- Claude Code Session 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab (2026-08-28 08:00:00Z) -->
78	```
79	
80	`--session-id` scans header UUIDs, not filenames or substring matches. One UUID
81	can have multiple rendered aliases. In that case the script returns
82	`status=ambiguous`, lists every candidate, exits 4, and requires an explicit
83	`--specstory-path` to disambiguate. When both selectors are supplied, the path's
84	header UUID must exactly equal `--session-id`.
85	
86	To render one known raw session explicitly with SpecStory 2.10:
87	
88	```bash
89	specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
90	```
91	
92	If that creates another alias for a UUID already present, select the intended
93	path explicitly; do not infer from its timestamp.
94	
95	## SpecStory 2.10 scoping: checkout path, not branch
96	
97	Verified behavior in SpecStory 2.10:
98	
99	- Rendered output discovery is scoped to the checkout path containing
100	  `.specstory/history/`, not to the checked-out branch name.
101	- Raw Claude session discovery is likewise scoped through the checkout path's
102	  Claude project slug, not its branch.
103	- Switching branches in one checkout therefore exposes the same session pool.
104	  Newest-file selection can pick a transcript produced on another branch.
105	- Two worktrees have different roots, SpecStory history directories, and Claude
106	  project slugs. Prefer **worktree first, wrapper/session second**.
107	- Run one SpecStory wrapper/session per change stream. If a stream moves, stop
108	  the old wrapper and start a new one in the target worktree.
109	- `EnterWorktree` changes the agent's working directory; it does **not** rebind a
110	  SpecStory watcher that was already running against another checkout.
111	
112	This is why branch identity never appears in the exact selector contract. The
113	stable tuple is checkout root + session UUID + rendered path when needed.
114	
115	## Structured output
116	
117	TSV is the default and always starts with resolution metadata:
118	
119	```text
120	status	resolved
121	confidence	exact
122	source	session-id+specstory-path
123	specstory_path	/absolute/checkout/.specstory/history/session.md
124	claude_session_uuid	01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
125	claude_jsonl_path	/absolute/home/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl
126	```
127	
128	Ambiguous or invalid selections add repeated `candidate<TAB>path` rows. `--json`
129	emits the same fields plus a `candidates` array as one JSON object. Diagnostics
130	go to stderr; `--quiet` suppresses those diagnostics without hiding structured
131	stdout.
132	
133	| Exit | Meaning |
134	|---:|---|
135	| 0 | Requested exact artifacts resolved, or explicit heuristic succeeded |
136	| 1 | Invalid/missing arguments |
137	| 2 | Not inside a git repository |
138	| 3 | Requested artifact not found |
139	| 4 | Exact UUID has multiple rendered candidates |
140	| 5 | Path, header, or JSONL identity mismatch |
141	
142	These nonzero exits are intentional. Callers must not convert absence or
143	ambiguity into an empty "success" and then guess.
144	
145	## Exact staging handoff
146	
147	`stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` calls this resolver before touching
148	the index. It requires exact identity plus exactly one of `--plan PATH` or
149	`--no-plan`; use `--no-specstory` only with `--session-id` when rendered output
150	is intentionally absent. Resolver failures map to staging exit 5 and leave the
151	index unchanged.
152	
153	The staging script's no-selector invocation remains broad branch-wide
154	compatibility mode. It stages all dirty Markdown under configured artifact
155	directories and does not claim session identity.
156	
157	## Cross-reference
158	
159	- [`pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](./pre-commit-redaction-stack.md) — how
160	  selected files are scanned and redacted at commit time.
161	- [`../scripts/find-session.sh`](../scripts/find-session.sh) — exact resolver.
162	- [`../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh`](../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh) —
163	  validation and one-shot index update.
164
```
</details></tool-use>

5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh`       | "Which harness/model + artifact trailers belong in it?"      |
19	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
20	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
21	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
22	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
23	
24	## Core invariants
25	
26	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
27	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
28	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
29	2. **SpecStory state is not review history.** Precisely ignore
30	   `.specstory/.project.json` (machine/path-derived identity) and
31	   `.specstory/statistics.json` (regenerable statistics), but never ignore
32	   `.specstory/` or `.specstory/history/` as a whole.
33	3. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
34	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
35	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
36	4. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
37	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
38	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
39	   history back.
40	4. **Provenance is derived from the staged snapshot.** Never point a commit
41	   trailer at an unstaged transcript/plan, and never guess an unknown model.
42	
43	## When to use this skill
44	
45	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
46	
47	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
48	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
49	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
50	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
51	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
52	- You see recurring `.specstory/.project.json` or
53	  `.specstory/statistics.json` churn, especially across machines.
54	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
55	  chat history".
56	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
57	  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
58	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
59	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
60	  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.
61	
62	## When NOT to use
63	
64	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
65	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
66	  skip this skill entirely.
67	- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
68	  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
69	- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
70	  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
71	- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
72	  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).
73	
74	## Integration with existing infrastructure
75	
76	This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
77	already has. It does not duplicate:
78	
79	- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
80	  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
81	  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
82	  config the wrapper expects to find.
83	- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
84	  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
85	  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
86	  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
87	  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
88	- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
89	  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
90	  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
91	  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
92	  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).
93	
94	What this skill **adds**:
95	
96	- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
97	- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
98	  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
99	- Exact checkout/session discovery (`find-session.sh`) with an explicit
100	  `--newest` compatibility escape hatch for the "find my transcript among
101	  many" problem.
102	- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
103	  committing.
104	
105	## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene
106	
107	Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
108	chat/plan artifacts.
109	
110	```bash
111	# 1. Take the UUID from Claude Code /status. If SpecStory produced more than
112	#    one alias for it, name the rendered path too.
113	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
114	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
115	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-agent-history-selectors.md'
116	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh \
117	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT"
118	
119	# 2. Stage code, then exactly one validated transcript/plan set.
120	git add path/to/feature/file.ts
121	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh \
122	  --session-only --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
123	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" --plan "$PLAN"
124	# Use --no-plan when no plan exists. Use --no-specstory with --session-id when
125	# rendered history is intentionally absent. The script never chooses a plan.
126	
127	# 3. Generate the canonical FINAL trailer block from staged artifacts.
128	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
129	
130	# 4. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
131	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
132	  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
133	  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
134	  exit 1
135	}
136	
137	# 5. Append that block after any native attribution, validate with the
138	#    git-workflow companion, then commit. pre-commit re-runs redaction/gitleaks.
139	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
140	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
141	git commit -F /path/to/commit-message.txt
142	```
143	
144	The no-selector invocation of `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` is deliberately kept as
145	**broad branch-wide compatibility mode**: it stages every dirty Markdown artifact
146	under `assets/artifact-dirs.txt`. Use it only when that broad set is intentional;
147	it is not a substitute for exact session identity.
148	
149	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
150	
151	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
152	installed. Runs once per repo.
153	
154	```bash
155	cd /path/to/new/project
156	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
157	  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit
158	
159	# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
160	pre-commit run --all-files
161	```
162	
163	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
164	
165	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
166	   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
167	   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
168	   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
169	   keeps it current everywhere.
170	2. Creates or merges `.specstory/.gitignore` with only these anchored rules:
171	
172	   ```gitignore
173	   /.project.json
174	   /statistics.json
175	   ```
176	
177	   This keeps machine-local identity and generated statistics out of Git
178	   without hiding `.specstory/history/`. If either state file is already
179	   tracked, bootstrap warns because ignore rules do not affect tracked files;
180	   re-run with `--untrack-specstory-state` to apply `git rm --cached` while
181	   keeping the local files on disk. Use `--dry-run` to preview it.
182	3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
183	   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
184	4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
185	   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
186	5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
187	   one-line patch if missing.
188	6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that stages only
189	   from explicit `AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID` / `AGENT_HISTORY_SPECSTORY_PATH`
190	   identity plus `AGENT_HISTORY_PLAN` or `AGENT_HISTORY_NO_PLAN=1` (and optional
191	   `AGENT_HISTORY_NO_SPECSTORY=1`). With no identity it prints a visible no-op;
192	   it never picks newest files. If `core.hooksPath` is configured, bootstrap
193	   fails before writing anything: `.git/hooks/` would be inactive, so the user
194	   must integrate the exact staging call into that configured directory or
195	   unset the override for the repo.
196	
197	Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
198	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):
199	
200	```bash
201	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
202	```
203	
204	removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
205	remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
206	(idempotent; safe to re-run).
207	
208	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
209	
210	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
211	committed / pushed a secret":
212	
213	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
214	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
215	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
216	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
217	   become worth discussing.
218	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
219	
220	## Gotchas
221	
222	- **`.gitignore` does not retroactively untrack files.** SpecStory's own
223	  nested ignore historically covered `.project.json` but not the later-added
224	  `statistics.json`, and either file may already be committed. Adding the two
225	  precise rules stops new files only. Run bootstrap with
226	  `--untrack-specstory-state` to stage their removal from Git while preserving
227	  both local files. Never compensate with `.specstory/` or
228	  `.specstory/history/` in an ignore file; that discards the review trail.
229	- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
230	  against it.** Since
231	  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
232	  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
233	  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
234	  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
235	  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
236	  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
237	  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
238	  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
239	  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
240	  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
241	  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
242	  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
243	  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
244	  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
245	  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
246	  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
247	  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
248	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
249	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
250	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
251	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
252	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
253	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
254	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
255	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
256	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
257	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
258	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
259	  syntax everywhere.
260	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
261	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
262	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
263	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
264	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
265	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
266	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
267	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
268	- **SpecStory 2.10 is checkout-path scoped, not branch scoped.** Both rendered
269	  output discovery and raw Claude session discovery follow the checkout path;
270	  switching branches in one checkout does not separate histories. Create the
271	  worktree first, then start one SpecStory wrapper/session per change stream.
272	  Use `specstory sync claude -s UUID` for an explicit raw session. One UUID can
273	  produce multiple rendered aliases, so `find-session.sh --session-id UUID`
274	  fails ambiguous until `--specstory-path` selects one. `EnterWorktree` does not
275	  rebind a SpecStory watcher that was already running; restart the wrapper in
276	  the target worktree.
277	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
278	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
279	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
280	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
281	  agent artifacts, not after.
282	- **`--install-hook` cannot bypass `core.hooksPath`.** Git reads hooks from the
283	  configured directory instead of `.git/hooks/`; writing a repo-local
284	  `prepare-commit-msg` there would silently do nothing. Bootstrap now exits 6
285	  before creating files and prints the two valid remedies. It never edits a
286	  user's global hook directory on their behalf.
287	- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
288	  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
289	  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
290	  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
291	  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
292	  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
293	  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
294	  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
295	  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
296	  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
297	  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
298	  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
299	  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
300	  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
301	  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
302	  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
303	  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
304	  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
305	  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
306	  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
307	  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
308	  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
309	  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
310	  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
311	  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
312	  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
313	  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
314	  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
315	  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
316	  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
317	  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
318	  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
319	  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).
320	
321	## Available scripts
322	
323	- **`scripts/find-session.sh (--session-id UUID | --specstory-path PATH | --newest) [--format specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
324	  Resolve from the git root. Exact mode verifies the SpecStory header plus the
325	  Claude JSONL filename and parsed `sessionId`/`cwd`; duplicate aliases report
326	  candidates and exit 4. TSV and JSON both include `status`, `confidence`, and
327	  `source`. Missing/mismatched identities fail closed; `--newest` is the only
328	  heuristic path.
329	
330	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only --session-id UUID|--specstory-path PATH (--plan PATH|--no-plan)] [--no-specstory] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
331	  Exact session-only mode validates every path before one `git add`; selector
332	  failures exit 5 with the index unchanged, and it never chooses the newest
333	  plan. The no-selector default preserves broad branch-wide compatibility by
334	  staging every dirty `*.md` in configured artifact directories. Refuses
335	  artifact-only work unless `--allow-empty` is explicit.
336	
337	- **`scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh [--harness NAME --model NAME] [--format trailers|json]`**
338	  Read staged SpecStory/plan artifacts and emit deduplicated
339	  `AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, and `Agent-Plan` values. Parses the
340	  staged blob rather than a concurrently-changing working-tree transcript;
341	  requires explicit harness+model overrides when it cannot prove them.
342	
343	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
344	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
345	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
346	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
347	
348	- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
349	  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
350	  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
351	  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
352	  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.
353	
354	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--untrack-specstory-state] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
355	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
356	  repo, merge precise SpecStory state ignores, wire the hook to the installed
357	  skill's redactor, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
358	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
359	  without hiding transcript directories. Already-tracked state is only
360	  untracked with the explicit flag; `--dry-run` previews that index change.
361	  `--install-hook` generates an explicit `AGENT_HISTORY_*` selector hook with a
362	  visible no-op when identity is absent, and exits 6 when `core.hooksPath` would
363	  make the repo-local hook inert.

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# find-session.sh — resolve the current agent session files for $PWD.
#
# Returns the SpecStory transcript path + Claude Code session UUID/JSONL
# path for the current working directory, so the calling agent can stage
# the right artifacts before a commit.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: find-session.sh [OPTIONS]

Discover the agent session files associated with $PWD. Heuristics:
  - SpecStory: newest *.md under ./.specstory/history/
  - Claude Code: newest *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ where
                 <slug> is $PWD with '/' -> '-' (Claude's own convention).

Options:
  --format=VALUE     one of: specstory, claude, both (default: both)
  --json             Emit JSON instead of TSV.
  --quiet            Suppress stderr diagnostics on empty results.
  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.

Output (TSV, one key/value per line):
  specstory_path       <abs path or empty>
  claude_session_uuid  <uuid or empty>
  claude_jsonl_path    <abs path or empty>

Exit codes:
  0  always (never fails the pipeline; empty values signal absence).
  1  invalid arguments.
EOF
}

log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

FORMAT="both"
OUT_JSON=0
QUIET=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
    --format)   FORMAT="${2:-both}"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)     OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
    --quiet)    QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)         die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)          die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
  esac
done

case "$FORMAT" in
  both|specstory|claude) ;;
  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
esac

# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with every NON-ALPHANUMERIC character
# replaced by '-' -- not just '/'.
#   /Volumes/Data/x          -> -Volumes-Data-x
#   /home/u/.local/share/foo -> -home-u--local-share-foo   (the dot collapses)
# The leading dash is intentional -- it mirrors how Claude Code names the
# subdirectory under ~/.claude/projects/. Using `tr '/' '-'` here silently
# returns an empty result for any path containing '.', '_' or a space.
cwd_slug() {
  printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9]|-|g'
}

newest_file() {
  # newest_file <dir> <glob>
  # Prints the newest matching file by mtime, or empty if none.
  local dir="$1" glob="$2"
  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
  # stat -f on macOS, stat -c on Linux — use find+sort for portability.
  local found
  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
    | head -n 1)
  printf '%s' "$found"
}

SPECSTORY_PATH=""
CLAUDE_JSONL=""
CLAUDE_UUID=""

if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
  candidate=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
    SPECSTORY_PATH="$candidate"
  else
    log "no .specstory/history/*.md under $PWD"
  fi
fi

if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
  slug=$(cwd_slug)
  proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$slug"
  candidate=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
    CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
    CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$candidate" .jsonl)
  else
    log "no ~/.claude/projects/$slug/*.jsonl (slug derived from PWD)"
  fi
fi

if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
  # Hand-rolled JSON keeps us dependency-free (no jq/python requirement).
  printf '{"specstory_path":"%s","claude_session_uuid":"%s","claude_jsonl_path":"%s"}\n' \
    "$SPECSTORY_PATH" "$CLAUDE_UUID" "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
else
  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
  printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
  printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
fi
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
# the next commit.
#
# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]

Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.

Options:
  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.

Exit codes:
  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
  1  invalid arguments
  2  not inside a git repo
  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

SESSION_ONLY=0
INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
DRY_RUN=0
ALLOW_EMPTY=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Must be in a git repo.
if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "not inside a git repo" 2
fi
REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
fi

ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  # Strip comments and whitespace.
  line="${line%%#*}"
  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
done < "$DIRS_FILE"

# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
check_ignored() {
  local dir="$1"
  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
  fi
}

# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
find_current_specstory() {
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
}
find_current_plan() {
  [ -d ".claude/plans" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
  find .claude/plans -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null \
    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
list_dirty_artifacts() {
  local dir path git_status
  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
    check_ignored "$dir"
    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
      # We only want the path portion.
      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
      path="${entry:3}"
      case "$path" in
        *.md) ;;
        *) continue ;;
      esac
      case "$git_status" in
        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
        "M "|"A ")
          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
          ;;
      esac
    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
  done
}

# --- Main ---
STAGED_COUNT=0
CANDIDATES=()

if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
  plan=$(find_current_plan)
  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
else
  # Capture the dirty artifact list.
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    CANDIDATES+=("$f")
  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
fi

# Check: are there code changes outside the artifact dirs?
# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
has_code_changes() {
  local any=0 line path in_artifact dir
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
    path="${line:3}"
    in_artifact=0
    for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
      case "$path" in
        "$dir"/*) in_artifact=1; break ;;
      esac
    done
    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$any" = "1" ]
}

if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  if has_code_changes; then
    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
    exit 0
  fi
  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
  exit 3
fi

if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
  exit 4
fi

# Stage (or print).
for f in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$f"
  else
    git add -- "$f"
    printf 'staged: %s\n' "$f"
  fi
  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))
done

log "${STAGED_COUNT} artifact(s) ${DRY_RUN:+would be }staged."
```
</details></tool-use>

287	  while IFS= read -r -d '' artifact; do
288	    append_unique_candidate "$artifact"
289	  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
290	fi
291	
292	# Complete path validation before any index mutation.
293	for artifact in "${CANDIDATES[@]:-}"; do
294	  [ -n "$artifact" ] || continue
295	  validate_candidate_path "$artifact"
296	done
297	
298	if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
299	  if has_code_changes; then
300	    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
301	    exit 0
302	  fi
303	  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
304	  exit 3
305	fi
306	
307	if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
308	  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes are present."
309	  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
310	  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if this artifact-only change is intentional."
311	  exit 4
312	fi
313	
314	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
315	  for artifact in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
316	    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$artifact"
317	  done
318	  log "${#CANDIDATES[@]} artifact(s) validated; index unchanged."
319	  exit 0
320	fi
321	
322	# One git process updates the index only after every selector/path check passed.
323	git add -- "${CANDIDATES[@]}"
324	for artifact in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
325	  printf 'staged: %s\n' "$artifact"
326	done
327	log "${#CANDIDATES[@]} artifact(s) staged atomically."

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban

23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
