65	```
66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	Active series in this repo:
76	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
77	
78	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
79	
80	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
81	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
82	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
83	
84	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
85	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
86	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
87	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
88	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
89	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
90	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
91	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
92	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
93	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
94	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
95	
96	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
97	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
98	
99	## Marketplace Catalog
100	
101	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
102	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
103	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
104	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
105	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
106	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
107	for the full mechanism.
108	
109	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
110	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
111	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
112	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
113	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
114	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
115	
116	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
117	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
118	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
119	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
120	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
121	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
122	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
123	within-group caveat in
124	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
125	
126	## SKILL.md Format
127	
128	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
129	
130	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
131	
132	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
133	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
134	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
135	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
136	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
137	
138	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
139	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
140	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
141	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
142	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
143	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
144	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
145	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
146	
147	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
148	
149	```bash
150	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
151	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
152	
153	# …or remove them afterward
154	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
155	```
156	
157	## Project Memory Workflow
158	
159	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
160	
161	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
162	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
163	
164	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
165	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
166	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
167	
168	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
169	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
170	
171	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
172	
173	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
174	
175	   ```bash
176	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
177	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
178	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
179	   ```
180	
181	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
182	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
183	
184	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
185	
186	   ```bash
187	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
191	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
192	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
193	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
194	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
195	
196	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
197	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
198	   afterwards to catch drift.
199	
200	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
201	
202	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
203	
204	```bash
205	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
206	```
207	
208	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
209	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
210	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
211	
212	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
213	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
214	
215	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
216	
217	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
218	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
219	own conventions). It has three subareas:
220	
221	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
222	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
223	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
224	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
225	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
226	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
227	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
228	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
229	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
230	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
231	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
232	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
233	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
234	  status / license / last_verified`).
235	
236	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
237	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
238	
239	| Status | Meaning |
240	|---|---|
241	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
242	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
243	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
244	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
245	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
246	
247	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
248	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
249	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
250	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
251	
252	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
253	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
254	
255	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
256	
257	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
258	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
259	
260	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
261	2. The root cause
262	3. The workaround
263	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
264	
265	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
266	the explanation they do not know yet.
267

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.9"
4	# dependencies = []
5	# ///
6	# NOTE: stdlib-only, so a plain `python3` shebang is the portable default
7	# (works on macOS system 3.9, CI, and as a pre-commit `language: script` hook
8	# with no uv dependency). The PEP 723 block above still lets you run it under
9	# `uv run --script redact_secrets.py` if you prefer an isolated interpreter.
10	"""
11	Check for secrets in agent artifact directories (specstory history + coding
12	agent plan/rules dirs) using gitleaks and detect-private-key patterns.
13	Reports findings and suggests redaction.
14	
15	Default covered prefixes (kept in sync with assets/artifact-dirs.txt):
16	    .specstory/history/   (SpecStory chat transcripts)
17	    .claude/plans/        (Claude Code plans)
18	    .cursor/plans/        (Cursor plans)
19	    .cursor/rules/        (Cursor rules)
20	    .opencode/plans/      (OpenCode plans)
21	    .specify/             (GitHub spec-kit artifacts)
22	    .codex/               (Codex CLI artifacts)
23	
24	Redacted secrets are replaced with `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the same sentinel
25	shape SpecStory >= 2.4.0 writes natively (its binary carries the format string
26	`[REDACTED:%s]`). Sharing one shape keeps the two layers idempotent: whichever
27	runs first, the other sees an inert placeholder and leaves the file alone. See
28	references/specstory-native-redaction.md for measured coverage of what
29	SpecStory already handles and what is left to us.
30

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12

14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync

31	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
32	make lint-frontmatter

34	# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
35	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
36	make validate

43	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill

46

66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	Active series in this repo:
76	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
77	
78	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
79	
80	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
81	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
82	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
83	
84	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
85	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
86	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
87	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
88	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
89	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
90	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
91	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
92	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
93	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
94	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
95	
96	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
97	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
98	
99	## Marketplace Catalog
100	
101	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
102	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
103	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
104	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
105	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
106	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
107	for the full mechanism.
108	
109	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
110	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
111	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
112	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
113	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
114	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
115	
116	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
117	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
118	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
119	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
120	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
121	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
122	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
123	within-group caveat in
124	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
125	
126	## SKILL.md Format
127	
128	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
129	
130	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
131	
132	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
133	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
134	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
135	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
136	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
137	
138	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
139	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
140	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
141	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
142	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
143	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
144	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
145	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
146	
147	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
148	
149	```bash
150	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
151	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
152	
153	# …or remove them afterward
154	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
155	```
156	
157	## Project Memory Workflow
158	
159	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
160	
161	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
162	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
163	
164	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
165	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
166	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
167	
168	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
169	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
170	
171	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
172	
173	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
174	
175	   ```bash
176	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
177	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
178	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
179	   ```
180	
181	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
182	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
183	
184	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
185	
186	   ```bash
187	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
191	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
192	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
193	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
194	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
195	
196	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
197	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
198	   afterwards to catch drift.
199	
200	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
201	
202	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
203	
204	```bash
205	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
206	```
207	
208	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
209	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
210	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
211	
212	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
213	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
214	
215	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
216	
217	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
218	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
219	own conventions). It has three subareas:
220	
221	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
222	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
223	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
224	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
225	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
226	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
227	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
228	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
229	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
230	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
231	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
232	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
233	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
234	  status / license / last_verified`).
235	
236	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
237	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
238	
239	| Status | Meaning |
240	|---|---|
241	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
242	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
243	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
244	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
245	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
246	
247	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
248	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
249	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
250	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
251	
252	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
253	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
254	
255	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
256	
257	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
258	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
259	
260	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
261	2. The root cause
262	3. The workaround
263	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
264	
265	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
266	the explanation they do not know yet.
267
```

```text
1	---
2	name: agent-history-hygiene
3	description: Commit SpecStory transcripts and Claude/Cursor/OpenCode/Codex plans with feature diffs, derive staged `AI-Assisted-By` plus transcript/plan trailers, prevent secret leaks, and ignore SpecStory machine-local state. Use when asked to commit/save/stage agent sessions, record cross-harness provenance, bootstrap pre-commit, fix `.specstory/statistics.json` churn, scrub a transcript, or remediate accidental secret commits/pushes with rotate-first discipline.
4	---
5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh`       | "Which harness/model + artifact trailers belong in it?"      |
19	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
20	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
21	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
22	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
23	
24	## Core invariants
25	
26	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
27	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
28	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
29	2. **SpecStory state is not review history.** Precisely ignore
30	   `.specstory/.project.json` (machine/path-derived identity) and
31	   `.specstory/statistics.json` (regenerable statistics), but never ignore
32	   `.specstory/` or `.specstory/history/` as a whole.
33	3. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
34	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
35	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
36	4. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
37	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
38	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
39	   history back.
40	4. **Provenance is derived from the staged snapshot.** Never point a commit
41	   trailer at an unstaged transcript/plan, and never guess an unknown model.
42	
43	## When to use this skill
44	
45	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
46	
47	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
48	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
49	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
50	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
51	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
52	- You see recurring `.specstory/.project.json` or
53	  `.specstory/statistics.json` churn, especially across machines.
54	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
55	  chat history".
56	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
57	  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
58	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
59	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
60	  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.
61	
62	## When NOT to use
63	
64	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
65	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
66	  skip this skill entirely.
67	- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
68	  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
69	- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
70	  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
71	- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
72	  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).
73	
74	## Integration with existing infrastructure
75	
76	This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
77	already has. It does not duplicate:
78	
79	- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
80	  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
81	  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
82	  config the wrapper expects to find.
83	- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
84	  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
85	  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
86	  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
87	  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
88	- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
89	  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
90	  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
91	  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
92	  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).
93	
94	What this skill **adds**:
95	
96	- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
97	- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
98	  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
99	- Exact checkout/session discovery (`find-session.sh`) with an explicit
100	  `--newest` compatibility escape hatch for the "find my transcript among
101	  many" problem.
102	- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
103	  committing.
104	
105	## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene
106	
107	Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
108	chat/plan artifacts.
109	
110	```bash
111	# 1. Take the UUID from Claude Code /status. If SpecStory produced more than
112	#    one alias for it, name the rendered path too.
113	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
114	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
115	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-agent-history-selectors.md'
116	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh \
117	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT"
118	
119	# 2. Stage code, then exactly one validated transcript/plan set.
120	git add path/to/feature/file.ts
121	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh \
122	  --session-only --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
123	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" --plan "$PLAN"
124	# Use --no-plan when no plan exists. Use --no-specstory with --session-id when
125	# rendered history is intentionally absent. The script never chooses a plan.
126	
127	# 3. Generate the canonical FINAL trailer block from staged artifacts.
128	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
129	
130	# 4. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
131	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
132	  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
133	  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
134	  exit 1
135	}
136	
137	# 5. Append that block after any native attribution, validate with the
138	#    git-workflow companion, then commit. pre-commit re-runs redaction/gitleaks.
139	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
140	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
141	git commit -F /path/to/commit-message.txt
142	```
143	
144	The no-selector invocation of `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` is deliberately kept as
145	**broad branch-wide compatibility mode**: it stages every dirty Markdown artifact
146	under `assets/artifact-dirs.txt`. Use it only when that broad set is intentional;
147	it is not a substitute for exact session identity.
148	
149	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
150	
151	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
152	installed. Runs once per repo.
153	
154	```bash
155	cd /path/to/new/project
156	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
157	  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit
158	
159	# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
160	pre-commit run --all-files
161	```
162	
163	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
164	
165	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
166	   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
167	   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
168	   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
169	   keeps it current everywhere.
170	2. Creates or merges `.specstory/.gitignore` with only these anchored rules:
171	
172	   ```gitignore
173	   /.project.json
174	   /statistics.json
175	   ```
176	
177	   This keeps machine-local identity and generated statistics out of Git
178	   without hiding `.specstory/history/`. If either state file is already
179	   tracked, bootstrap warns because ignore rules do not affect tracked files;
180	   re-run with `--untrack-specstory-state` to apply `git rm --cached` while
181	   keeping the local files on disk. Use `--dry-run` to preview it.
182	3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
183	   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
184	4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
185	   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
186	5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
187	   one-line patch if missing.
188	6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that stages only
189	   from explicit `AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID` / `AGENT_HISTORY_SPECSTORY_PATH`
190	   identity plus `AGENT_HISTORY_PLAN` or `AGENT_HISTORY_NO_PLAN=1` (and optional
191	   `AGENT_HISTORY_NO_SPECSTORY=1`). With no identity it prints a visible no-op;
192	   it never picks newest files. If `core.hooksPath` is configured, bootstrap
193	   fails before writing anything: `.git/hooks/` would be inactive, so the user
194	   must integrate the exact staging call into that configured directory or
195	   unset the override for the repo.
196	
197	Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
198	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):
199	
200	```bash
201	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
202	```
203	
204	removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
205	remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
206	(idempotent; safe to re-run).
207	
208	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
209	
210	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
211	committed / pushed a secret":
212	
213	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
214	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
215	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
216	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
217	   become worth discussing.
218	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
219	
220	## Gotchas
221	
222	- **`.gitignore` does not retroactively untrack files.** SpecStory's own
223	  nested ignore historically covered `.project.json` but not the later-added
224	  `statistics.json`, and either file may already be committed. Adding the two
225	  precise rules stops new files only. Run bootstrap with
226	  `--untrack-specstory-state` to stage their removal from Git while preserving
227	  both local files. Never compensate with `.specstory/` or
228	  `.specstory/history/` in an ignore file; that discards the review trail.
229	- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
230	  against it.** Since
231	  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
232	  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
233	  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
234	  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
235	  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
236	  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
237	  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
238	  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
239	  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
240	  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
241	  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
242	  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
243	  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
244	  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
245	  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
246	  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
247	  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
248	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
249	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
250	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
251	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
252	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
253	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
254	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
255	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
256	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
257	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
258	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
259	  syntax everywhere.
260	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
261	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
262	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
263	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
264	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
265	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
266	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
267	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
268	- **SpecStory 2.10 is checkout-path scoped, not branch scoped.** Both rendered
269	  output discovery and raw Claude session discovery follow the checkout path;
270	  switching branches in one checkout does not separate histories. Create the
271	  worktree first, then start one SpecStory wrapper/session per change stream.
272	  Use `specstory sync claude -s UUID` for an explicit raw session. One UUID can
273	  produce multiple rendered aliases, so `find-session.sh --session-id UUID`
274	  fails ambiguous until `--specstory-path` selects one. `EnterWorktree` does not
275	  rebind a SpecStory watcher that was already running; restart the wrapper in
276	  the target worktree.
277	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
278	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
279	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
280	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
281	  agent artifacts, not after.
282	- **`--install-hook` cannot bypass `core.hooksPath`.** Git reads hooks from the
283	  configured directory instead of `.git/hooks/`; writing a repo-local
284	  `prepare-commit-msg` there would silently do nothing. Bootstrap now exits 6
285	  before creating files and prints the two valid remedies. It never edits a
286	  user's global hook directory on their behalf.
287	- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
288	  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
289	  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
290	  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
291	  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
292	  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
293	  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
294	  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
295	  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
296	  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
297	  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
298	  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
299	  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
300	  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
301	  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
302	  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
303	  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
304	  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
305	  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
306	  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
307	  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
308	  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
309	  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
310	  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
311	  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
312	  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
313	  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
314	  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
315	  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
316	  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
317	  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
318	  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
319	  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).
320	
321	## Available scripts
322	
323	- **`scripts/find-session.sh (--session-id UUID | --specstory-path PATH | --newest) [--format specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
324	  Resolve from the git root. Exact mode verifies the SpecStory header plus the
325	  Claude JSONL filename and parsed `sessionId`/`cwd`; duplicate aliases report
326	  candidates and exit 4. TSV and JSON both include `status`, `confidence`, and
327	  `source`. Missing/mismatched identities fail closed; `--newest` is the only
328	  heuristic path.
329	
330	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only --session-id UUID|--specstory-path PATH (--plan PATH|--no-plan)] [--no-specstory] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
331	  Exact session-only mode validates every path before one `git add`; selector
332	  failures exit 5 with the index unchanged, and it never chooses the newest
333	  plan. The no-selector default preserves broad branch-wide compatibility by
334	  staging every dirty `*.md` in configured artifact directories. Refuses
335	  artifact-only work unless `--allow-empty` is explicit.
336	
337	- **`scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh [--harness NAME --model NAME] [--format trailers|json]`**
338	  Read staged SpecStory/plan artifacts and emit deduplicated
339	  `AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, and `Agent-Plan` values. Parses the
340	  staged blob rather than a concurrently-changing working-tree transcript;
341	  requires explicit harness+model overrides when it cannot prove them.
342	
343	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
344	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
345	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
346	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
347	
348	- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
349	  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
350	  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
351	  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
352	  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.
353	
354	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--untrack-specstory-state] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
355	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
356	  repo, merge precise SpecStory state ignores, wire the hook to the installed
357	  skill's redactor, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
358	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
359	  without hiding transcript directories. Already-tracked state is only
360	  untracked with the explicit flag; `--dry-run` previews that index change.
361	  `--install-hook` generates an explicit `AGENT_HISTORY_*` selector hook with a
362	  visible no-op when identity is absent, and exits 6 when `core.hooksPath` would
363	  make the repo-local hook inert.

+## SpecStory 2.10 checkout scoping
+
+Verified with SpecStory 2.10: rendered output discovery and raw Claude session
+discovery are scoped by **checkout path, not branch**. Switching branches in one
+checkout shares the same artifact pool; separate worktrees have separate
+`.specstory/history/` roots and Claude project slugs.
+
+Use **worktree first, wrapper/session second**, with one SpecStory wrapper and
+Claude session per change stream. Render a known raw session explicitly with:

+a newest-file tie-break: pass `--specstory-path`. `EnterWorktree` does not
+rebind a SpecStory watcher that is already running, so stop it and start a new
+wrapper in the target worktree.

 ## Post-leak discipline
 
 `scan-staged.sh` exit codes branch on leak state (0 clean, 10 redacted,
 20 leaks, 30 no gitleaks). When a leak slips through:
 
 1. **Rotate at the provider.** The only act that revokes the
    credential. Links in `references/remediation.md` §1.
 2. **Assess blast radius.** Local/unpushed? Feature branch? Main?
 3. **Scrub only if cheap.** Amend or `reset --soft` on unpushed commits;
    `git filter-repo` + force-with-lease on feature branches; **never**
    rewrite `main`.
 
 The runbook explicitly forbids `git push --force` against shared
 branches — see `references/remediation.md` §5.
 
 ## Gotchas
 
+- Branch names do not scope SpecStory 2.10 or Claude raw-session discovery;
+  checkout paths do. Never use `--newest` to infer a commit's exact session.
 - A configured `core.hooksPath` makes `.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` inert.
   `bootstrap-project.sh --install-hook` now exits 6 instead of installing a
   hook that Git will never execute.
 - Native Claude/Cursor attribution is additive. The portable minimum is the
   final `AI-Assisted-By` + transcript/plan block; do not invent an AI email or
   confuse message attribution with cryptographic signing.
 
 - SpecStory ≥ 2.4.0 already redacts on write — don't let the hook redo it.
   See [SpecStory native redaction](#specstory-native-redaction-v240) above.
 - A bare "PRIVATE KEY" mention is not a leak; `detect-private-key` matches
   `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` only. Redacting prose churned transcripts for nothing.
 - Claude Code `plansDirectory` project-level is sometimes ignored
   ([issue #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537));
   set at the user level (`~/.claude/settings.json`) as the default.
 - `gitleaks protect` is deprecated since v8.19.0 — use `gitleaks git
   --staged`. The skill uses the modern syntax everywhere.
 - `pre-commit install` is per-clone — each teammate (and CI) must run
   it for hooks to fire.
 - Global `core.hooksPath` runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
   only if it exists; a bare repo is unprotected until bootstrap.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

Two standing rules: every run that exercises the model spends real money, so get the user's approval first; and when context for a lever is missing, work through it interactively with the user - this workflow is not expected to one-shot the audit. ## Language Detection

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in (exception: for the `prompt-audit` subcommand, skip this section's ask steps - the audit is non-interactive and its inventory is language-agnostic; when no language is inferable, proceed without asking and state the assumption in the report):

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:

   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` -> **Python** - read from `python/`
   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` -> **TypeScript** - read from `typescript/`
   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) -> **TypeScript** - JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` -> **Java** - read from `java/`
   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` -> **Java** - Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` -> **Java** - Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.go`, `go.mod` -> **Go** - read from `go/`
   - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` -> **Ruby** - read from `ruby/`
   - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` -> **C#** - read from `csharp/`
   - `*.php`, `composer.json` -> **PHP** - read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

   - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
   - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

   - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP
   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

   - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) - Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases - only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** - scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute - file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice - use the tool runner for the agentic loop - its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) - or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity - see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` - that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* - you still host and deploy them yourself - which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API - manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop - no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API - Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** - *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1-3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs - see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner != Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request -> execute -> loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox - you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only - you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries - but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment - that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1-3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) - don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** - Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** - Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** - Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** - Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint - not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** - You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** - Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** - Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** - Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` - see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` - live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

### Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`) - most capable widely released model

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work; everything below also applies to **Claude Mythos 5** (`claude-mythos-5`, Project Glasswing - same capabilities, pricing, and API surface; successor to the invitation-only `claude-mythos-preview`). 1M context window (the maximum is also the default), 128K max output. Key API differences from Opus-tier - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5 for details:

- **Thinking is always on** - omit the `thinking` parameter entirely (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`). Any other explicit configuration is rejected: `{type: "disabled"}` and `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` both return a 400. Control depth with `output_config.effort` (supports `low` through `xhigh` and `max`).
- **The raw chain of thought is never returned** - responses carry regular `thinking` blocks (not `redacted_thinking`): `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary, `"omitted"` (the default) leaves the `thinking` field as an empty string. Replay rules: pass thinking blocks back unchanged on the same model; other models drop them silently (unbilled - nothing to strip); details in `shared/model-migration.md`.
- **Tokenizer** - same tokenizer as Opus 4.8 (introduced with Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from Opus 4.7/4.8; per-token pricing differs. Coming from Opus 4.6, Sonnet, Haiku, or older, re-baseline with `count_tokens` (the Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses ~1×-1.35× as many tokens).
- **`refusal` stop reason - handle it, and opt into fallbacks by default** - safety classifiers may decline a request (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: "refusal"`, with a `stop_details` category); always check `stop_reason` before reading `content`. **When you write `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` code, include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter by default.** Simplest form: `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` + `fallbacks: "default"`, which routes by refusal category so you never maintain a model list. (The older array form - `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"]` + `fallbacks: [{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}]` - still works; Claude API and Claude Platform on AWS - on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, use the SDKs' client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` + `BetaFallbackState`). Tell the user you've enabled it; drop it only if they decline. Full semantics (billing, mid-stream refusals, credit repricing) in `shared/model-migration.md` -> refusal section. **Per-language code examples in `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` § Refusal Fallbacks cover the array form only** - for the `"default"` mode, follow the raw-HTTP shape in `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Opus 5 -> New API features and swap `fallbacks: [{...}]` for `fallbacks: "default"` plus the `-2026-07-01` header; the rest of the request is unchanged.
- **No assistant prefill** - same as the rest of the 4.6+ family.
- **30-day data retention required** - Claude Fable 5 is not available under zero data retention; requests from an org whose retention configuration doesn't meet the requirement return `400 invalid_request_error`.
- **Longer turns, different prompting** - single requests on hard tasks can run many minutes (plan timeouts/streaming/progress UX); effort sweeps should include low/medium for routine work; prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive and reduce output quality. See `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5 -> Behavioral shifts (prompt-tunable) for the recommended prompt snippets.

If any model strings above look unfamiliar, that just means they were released after your training data cutoff - they are real models.

## Authentication (Quick Reference)

**An unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does NOT mean there are no credentials.** The SDKs and the `ant` CLI resolve credentials in this order (first match wins): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` -> `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` -> the `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`-selected or active OAuth profile from `ant auth login` -> Workload Identity Federation env vars -> the default profile on disk. A bare `Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` works after `ant auth login` with no env var set.

**When you need to call the API and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, don't ask the user for a key.** First run `ant auth status` - it shows which credential source and profile is active. If it reports an active profile:

- **SDK code or `ant` CLI:** just run it. The zero-arg client constructor and every `ant ...` subcommand pick up the profile automatically - no env var needed.
- **Raw `curl` / HTTP:** get a short-lived token with `ant auth print-credentials --access-token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` **plus** the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (OAuth tokens go on `Authorization: Bearer`, not `x-api-key:` - converting a curl from an API key is a header change, not a key swap). Always pass `--access-token`; the no-flag form prints JSON, not a bare token.

Only ask the user for a key if `ant auth status` reports no active credential source (or `ant` itself isn't installed). Suggest `ant auth login` as the first option - it stores a profile under `~/.config/anthropic/` that the SDKs read automatically - and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the alternative.

Full auth details (named profiles, scopes, the API-key-shadows-profile trap, refresh-token expiry): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.

## Thinking & Effort (Quick Reference)

Use adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) on every current model - Claude dynamically decides when and how much to think. Per-model rules:

| Model | Thinking config | Omitting `thinking` | `budget_tokens` | Sampling (`temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`) | Effort levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; explicit `{type: "disabled"}` returns 400 - omit the param instead | Runs adaptive (thinking is always on) | Removed - `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` returns 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Claude Opus 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted **only at effort `high` or below** - 400 at `xhigh`/`max`, and see the disabled-thinking pitfall below | Runs **adaptive** (thinking is on by default - unlike Opus 4.8/4.7) | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`-`max` (all five) |
| Opus 4.8 / 4.7 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs **without** thinking - set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Sonnet 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs adaptive | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 | `{type: "adaptive"}` (recommended; auto-enables interleaved thinking, no beta header) | Set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Deprecated - do not use in new code; transitional escape hatch only (see below) | Allowed | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`max` (`xhigh` arrived with Opus 4.7) |
| Older (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, ...) - only if explicitly requested | `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | No thinking | Required for thinking; must be less than `max_tokens`, minimum 1024 - errors otherwise | Allowed | `effort` works on Opus 4.5 (`low`/`medium`/`high` only - no `xhigh`/`max`); errors on Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 |

Opus 4.8 keeps the same request surface as 4.7 (no new breaking changes) - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Opus 4.8 for the behavioral re-tuning, and -> Migrating to Opus 4.7 for the full breaking-change list when coming from 4.6 or earlier. With `thinking` disabled, Opus 4.8 may write longer reasoning into the visible response - leave adaptive thinking on, or add a final-answer-only instruction (see the migration guide).

- **Effort (GA, no beta header):** `output_config: {effort: "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max"}` - inside `output_config`, not top-level; default `high` (equivalent to omitting it). Controls thinking depth and overall token spend; combine with adaptive thinking for the best cost-quality tradeoffs. `xhigh` (added on Opus 4.7, between `high` and `max`) is the best setting for most coding and agentic use cases on Fable 5 / Opus 4.7/4.8 / Sonnet 5, and the default in Claude Code; effort matters more on those models than on any prior model in their tier - re-tune it when migrating, and run long-horizon/agentic tasks at `high`/`xhigh` with the full task spec given up front. Use a minimum of `high` for intelligence-sensitive work, `max` when correctness matters more than cost, and `low` for subagents or simple tasks - lower effort means fewer and more-consolidated tool calls, less preamble, and terser confirmations (`high` is often the sweet spot balancing quality and token efficiency).
- **Choosing an effort level (cost tuning):** Effort is the first quality-trading lever, after the free wins (caching first) - it trades thoroughness against token spend within one model, and the top of the range earns its cost only on hard problems (raise to `max` only when measurement shows headroom at the level below). Which workloads repay higher effort is a property of the workload: coding and long-horizon agentic work respond strongly; chat, classification, and high-volume or latency-sensitive routes often don't and do well at `low`, with `medium` as the cost-saving step-down where quality holds (the per-level defaults above cover the rest). Measure on a sample of real requests before raising a default, and tune per route rather than globally. Before building a multi-model cost cascade, measure the simpler alternative first - the most capable model at lower effort on the same tasks: lower effort on the newest models often matches or exceeds prior-generation performance at high effort (on Fable 5, lower effort often exceeds `xhigh` on prior models), and one model means one cache namespace (caches are model-scoped, so a cascade forfeits cache reuse across its models; a mid-conversation `effort` change still invalidates the messages cache - `shared/prompt-caching.md` § Invalidation hierarchy). Judge cost per completed task, not per request - a cheaper request that needs more turns or retries to finish the job isn't cheaper. For the measured effort/cost tradeoffs by workload and the full lever order, `shared/cost-optimization.md` § 2.6.
- **Thinking display - `"omitted"` by default on Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / Sonnet 5:** `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary of the reasoning; `"omitted"` (the default on all six - a silent change from Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, where it was `"summarized"`) streams `thinking` blocks with empty text. `display` controls visibility only - thinking happens and is billed the same under every setting; the raw chain of thought is never exposed on any model. If you stream reasoning to users, the default looks like a long pause before output - set `thinking: {type: "adaptive", display: "summarized"}` explicitly. (Independent of display, echo thinking blocks back unchanged when continuing on the same model; other models silently ignore them - see the migration guide.)
- **When the user asks for "extended thinking", a "thinking budget", or `budget_tokens`:** always use Fable 5, Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, or 4.6 with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` - the fixed thinking-token-budget concept is deprecated and adaptive thinking replaces it. Do NOT use `budget_tokens` for new 4.6/4.7/4.8 code and do NOT switch to an older model just because the user mentions it. *Gradual-migration carve-out:* `budget_tokens` is still functional on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 only, as a transitional escape hatch for existing code that needs a hard token ceiling before you've tuned `effort` - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Transitional escape hatch. It is fully removed on Fable 5, Opus 5/4.7/4.8, and Sonnet 5.
