 `./docs/skills/agent-history-hygiene.md`

```text
1	# agent-history-hygiene
2	
3	Keep coding-agent chat transcripts and plan files committed alongside
4	the feature diff they produced, without leaking `.env` contents or API
5	keys into git history.
6	
7	| Surface | Question it answers |
8	|---|---|
9	| `find-session.sh` | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?" |
10	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?" |
11	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh` | "Which harness/model and artifact trailers belong in it?" |
12	| `bootstrap-project.sh` | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a new repo?" |
13	| `scan-staged.sh` | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?" |
14	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py` | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?" |
15	| `references/remediation.md` | "I already pushed a secret — now what?" |
16	
17	The skill exists to stop three common failure modes:
18	
19	1. Agents silently **dropping** `.specstory/history/*.md` and
20	   `.claude/plans/*.md` from commits because they look like generated
21	   artifacts.
22	2. Accidental `.env` echoes inside chat transcripts that then get
23	   committed and pushed.
24	3. Reflexive `git push --force` after a leak — which doesn't actually
25	   revoke the credential and often destroys teammate work.
26	
27	## When the skill triggers
28	
29	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "stage the plan
30	  file" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
31	- Untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` during a
32	  `git status`.
33	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
34	  chat history".
35	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "bootstrap secret scanning".
36	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" — the skill steers to
37	  the rotate-first runbook instead of a history rewrite.
38	
39	## Structure
40	
41	```
42	skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/
43	├── SKILL.md                                  # agent-facing workflow and invariants
44	├── scripts/
45	│   ├── find-session.sh                       # locate current SpecStory + Claude session
46	│   ├── stage-agent-artifacts.sh              # git-add the right artifacts
47	│   ├── agent-commit-metadata.sh               # derive staged provenance trailers
48	│   ├── bootstrap-project.sh                  # install pre-commit + gitleaks, wire the redactor
49	│   ├── probe-specstory-redaction.py          # measure SpecStory's own redaction coverage
50	│   └── scan-staged.sh                        # gitleaks wrapper with agent-friendly exit codes
51	├── references/
52	│   ├── transcript-session-discovery.md       # SpecStory / Claude session layouts
53	│   ├── pre-commit-redaction-stack.md         # layered defense design
54	│   ├── specstory-native-redaction.md         # what upstream redacts, measured
55	│   └── remediation.md                        # rotate-first leak runbook
56	└── assets/
57	    ├── artifact-dirs.txt                     # configurable list of agent artifact dirs
58	    ├── pre-commit-config.yaml.template
59	    ├── gitleaks.toml.template
60	    └── redact_secrets.py                     # run in place from the installed skill
61	```
62	
63	## Integration with chezmoi
64	
65	The skill sits on top of the user's existing chezmoi infrastructure
66	(if present):
67	
68	- `~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit` (global `core.hooksPath`) runs the
69	  repo-level `.pre-commit-config.yaml` this skill installs.
70	- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/redact_secrets.py` was the original
71	  upstream. `assets/redact_secrets.py` is now the source of truth and reaches
72	  consuming repos as a **pinned pre-commit hook** published from this repo's
73	  root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` — no vendored copy to drift.
74	  `bootstrap-project.sh --from-chezmoi` still symlinks the chezmoi
75	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml` for repos that prefer it.
76	- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.gitleaks.toml` shares rule IDs with the
77	  skill's `gitleaks.toml.template` so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist
78	  tweaks stay portable across repos.
79	
80	For repos without chezmoi, `bootstrap-project.sh` produces a
81	self-contained stack. The redactor is **not** copied into the repo: the
82	generated `.pre-commit-config.yaml` references the hook by tag, so
83	`pre-commit autoupdate` ships fixes everywhere and the script path never
84	depends on where `npx skills` happened to install the skill.
85	
86	```yaml
87	- repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
88	  rev: ahh-v1.1.0
89	  hooks:
90	    - id: redact-agent-secrets
91	```
92	
93	`bootstrap-project.sh --migrate` converts a repo off the old vendored
94	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` layout.
95	
96	`--install-hook` refuses to run when `core.hooksPath` redirects Git away from
97	`.git/hooks/`. It exits before writing bootstrap files and tells the user to
98	integrate the hook into the configured directory or unset the override for that
99	repo; the skill never edits a global hook directory on the user's behalf. The
100	generated hook never guesses: it stages only from explicit
101	`AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID` / `AGENT_HISTORY_SPECSTORY_PATH` plus
102	`AGENT_HISTORY_PLAN` or `AGENT_HISTORY_NO_PLAN=1` (and optional
103	`AGENT_HISTORY_NO_SPECSTORY=1`). With no identity, it prints a visible no-op.
104	
105	## Default workflow: commit feature + chat together
106	
107	```bash
108	# 1. Get the UUID from Claude Code /status and name the rendered alias.
109	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
110	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
111	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-agent-history-selectors.md'
112	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh \
113	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT"
114	
115	# 2. Stage code, then exactly one validated transcript/plan set.
116	git add path/to/feature.ts
117	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh \
118	  --session-only --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
119	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" --plan "$PLAN"
120	# Use --no-plan when no plan exists. Use --no-specstory with --session-id only
121	# when rendered output is intentionally absent. No plan is chosen by mtime.
122	
123	# 3. Generate the canonical final trailer block from staged artifacts.
124	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
125	
126	# 4. Scan secrets and validate the complete English message.
127	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
128	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
129	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
130	
131	# 5. Commit. Pre-commit re-runs redact + gitleaks as a catch-all.
132	git commit -F /path/to/commit-message.txt
133	```
134	
135	The metadata helper reads staged blobs, not concurrently-changing working
136	files. It emits deduplicated `AI-Assisted-By: Harness (model)`,
137	`Agent-Transcript`, and conditional `Agent-Plan` trailers. Pass explicit
138	`--harness` + `--model` only when a transcript cannot prove that identity.
139	
140	`find-session.sh` is exact by default. It anchors at the git root, validates an
141	exact SpecStory `Claude Code Session UUID` header, and parses the selected raw
142	Claude JSONL for an exact `sessionId` + `cwd`. TSV and `--json` output include
143	`status`, `confidence`, `source`, selected paths, and ambiguity candidates.
144	Missing artifacts, duplicate UUID aliases, and identity mismatches return
145	nonzero; `--newest` is the only heuristic mode.
146	
147	`stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` validates all selectors and paths
148	before one `git add`. Selector failures exit 5 with the index unchanged. The
149	no-selector command remains **broad branch-wide compatibility mode** and stages
150	every dirty Markdown artifact under configured directories; use it only when
151	that whole set is intentional.
152	
153	## SpecStory 2.10 checkout scoping
154	
155	Verified with SpecStory 2.10: rendered output discovery and raw Claude session
156	discovery are scoped by **checkout path, not branch**. Switching branches in one
157	checkout shares the same artifact pool; separate worktrees have separate
158	`.specstory/history/` roots and Claude project slugs.
159	
160	Use **worktree first, wrapper/session second**, with one SpecStory wrapper and
161	Claude session per change stream. Render a known raw session explicitly with:
162	
163	```bash
164	specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
165	```
166	
167	The same UUID can produce multiple rendered aliases. That is an ambiguity, not
168	a newest-file tie-break: pass `--specstory-path`. `EnterWorktree` does not
169	rebind a SpecStory watcher that is already running, so stop it and start a new
170	wrapper in the target worktree.
171	
172	## SpecStory native redaction (v2.4.0+)
173	
174	SpecStory ships its own secret redaction now, so this skill is no longer the
175	first line of defense for `.specstory/history/`.
176	
177	| Ref | What |
178	|---|---|
179	| [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) | `feat(redaction): automatically redact secrets from saved markdown history` — community PR by [@warnes](https://github.com/warnes), merged 2026-07-20 |
180	| [PR #253](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/253) | A `gofmt` CI-fix fork of #235; closed in favor of #235 |
181	| **v2.4.0** (2026-07-20) | Shipped **on by default**, via the [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset, covering local markdown **and** cloud sync |
182	| [#274](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/274) (open) | Adjacent leak vector — `specstory watch` exposes the cloud auth token in its process command line |
183	
184	The merged code is not the PR's: the maintainer swapped its 11 inline regexes
185	for Betterleaks, and the PR's `extra_patterns` (custom regexes) did not survive
186	that rewrite. `[redaction] enabled` in `.specstory/cli/config.toml` — or
187	`--no-redact-secrets` — is the only knob.
188	
189	### Measured coverage
190	
191	`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py` synthesizes a Claude Code session,
192	renders it twice through `specstory sync --print` (with and without
193	`--no-redact-secrets`), and diffs per secret class. Against specstory 2.9.0,
194	over 54 class/context pairs:
195	
196	| Caught by | Pairs | Examples |
197	|---|---:|---|
198	| SpecStory | 36 | Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub PAT/OAuth/Actions, GitLab, Google, Groq, Slack, Stripe, Supabase, Linear, PEM blocks, `.env` dumps |
199	| **Ours only** | 15 | Cursor, Tailscale, Discord/Zapier/Make webhooks — plus HuggingFace, Notion, WakaTime, OpenAI project keys **in prose** |
200	| Nobody | 3 | `AKIA…` access key IDs; Telegram bot tokens in prose |
201	
202	The structural finding: Betterleaks catches several classes only in
203	`KEY=value` form, via an entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule. The same token
204	in a sentence — which is how a tool transcript actually prints one — sails
205	through. Our prefix-anchored rules don't care about surrounding syntax.
206	
207	### How the two layers stay out of each other's way
208	
209	Both write the same sentinel, `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` (SpecStory's binary
210	carries the format string `[REDACTED:%s]`), and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists
211	that shape. A transcript SpecStory already cleaned passes through the hook
212	untouched — no "files were modified by this hook", no re-`git add`, no second
213	commit.
214	
215	The redactor writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` instead of `sk-abc...xyz`
216	truncations, and PEM blocks become `[REDACTED:private-key]` — the exact label
217	SpecStory uses. The truncated form still appears in the console report, where a
218	fingerprint helps identify which credential to rotate. `--legacy` writes the
219	pre-2.4.0 placeholders instead; it changes only the bytes written, never what
220	is detected.
221	
222	(The related rule that a bare `PRIVATE KEY` *mention* is not key material —
223	`detect-private-key` greps for `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` headers — is enforced
224	separately by the redactor's header-scoped matching.)
225	
226	## Post-leak discipline
227	
228	`scan-staged.sh` exit codes branch on leak state (0 clean, 10 redacted,
229	20 leaks, 30 no gitleaks). When a leak slips through:
230	
231	1. **Rotate at the provider.** The only act that revokes the
232	   credential. Links in `references/remediation.md` §1.
233	2. **Assess blast radius.** Local/unpushed? Feature branch? Main?
234	3. **Scrub only if cheap.** Amend or `reset --soft` on unpushed commits;
235	   `git filter-repo` + force-with-lease on feature branches; **never**
236	   rewrite `main`.
237	
238	The runbook explicitly forbids `git push --force` against shared
239	branches — see `references/remediation.md` §5.
240	
241	## Gotchas
242	
243	- Branch names do not scope SpecStory 2.10 or Claude raw-session discovery;
244	  checkout paths do. Never use `--newest` to infer a commit's exact session.
245	- A configured `core.hooksPath` makes `.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` inert.
246	  `bootstrap-project.sh --install-hook` now exits 6 instead of installing a
247	  hook that Git will never execute.
248	- Native Claude/Cursor attribution is additive. The portable minimum is the
249	  final `AI-Assisted-By` + transcript/plan block; do not invent an AI email or
250	  confuse message attribution with cryptographic signing.
251	
252	- SpecStory ≥ 2.4.0 already redacts on write — don't let the hook redo it.
253	  See [SpecStory native redaction](#specstory-native-redaction-v240) above.
254	- A bare "PRIVATE KEY" mention is not a leak; `detect-private-key` matches
255	  `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` only. Redacting prose churned transcripts for nothing.
256	- Claude Code `plansDirectory` project-level is sometimes ignored
257	  ([issue #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537));
258	  set at the user level (`~/.claude/settings.json`) as the default.
259	- `gitleaks protect` is deprecated since v8.19.0 — use `gitleaks git
260	  --staged`. The skill uses the modern syntax everywhere.
261	- `pre-commit install` is per-clone — each teammate (and CI) must run
262	  it for hooks to fire.
263	- Global `core.hooksPath` runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
264	  only if it exists; a bare repo is unprotected until bootstrap.
265	
266	## See also
267	
268	- [Source](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene)
269	- [`project-knowledge-harness`](project-knowledge-harness.md) —
270	  complementary memory harness that references `.claude/plans/` as
271	  ephemeral scratchpads. This skill closes the loop by making sure
272	  those scratchpads actually land in git.
273
```

8	把 coding agent 的對話 transcript 與 plan 檔，跟它們產生的功能 diff 一起
9	commit，且不讓 `.env` 內容或 API key 漏到 git 歷史。
10	
11	| 介面 (Surface) | 它回答的問題 |
12	|---|---|
13	| `find-session.sh` | 「**我**目前 session 的 transcript / plan 是哪一個？」 |
14	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` | 「下次 commit 應該包含哪些 agent 檔？」 |
15	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh` | 「這次 commit 該帶哪些 harness/model 與 artifact trailers？」 |
16	| `bootstrap-project.sh` | 「怎麼把 pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor 裝進新 repo？」 |
17	| `scan-staged.sh` | 「我準備 commit 的東西裡有沒有洩漏的 secret？」 |
18	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py` | 「SpecStory 自己已經 redact 了什麼，我們不用重做？」 |
19	| `references/remediation.md` | 「我已經 push 了 secret —— 現在怎麼辦？」 |

21	這個 skill 的存在是為了阻止三種常見失敗：
22	
23	1. Agent 因為把 `.specstory/history/*.md` 跟 `.claude/plans/*.md` 看成
24	   生成 (generated) 產物，**默默地**從 commit 中漏掉它們。
25	2. 對話 transcript 中意外的 `.env` echo，被 commit 並 push 出去。
26	3. 洩漏後的 reflexive `git push --force` —— 它根本不會撤銷憑證
27	   (credential)，反而常常毀掉隊友的工作。
28

30	
31	- 「Commit my chat」/「save the specstory session」/「stage the plan
32	  file」/「把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去」。
33	- `git status` 中出現未追蹤的 `.specstory/history/*.md` 或
34	  `.claude/plans/*.md`。
35	- 「Scrub this transcript」/「redact my key」/「gitleaks flagged my
36	  chat history」。
37	- 「Set up pre-commit for this repo」/「bootstrap secret scanning」。
38	- 「I pushed a `.env`」/「a secret went to main」 —— skill 會把使用者
39	  導向 rotate-first runbook，而不是去做歷史改寫。

104	## 預設工作流程：把功能跟對話一起 commit
105	
106	```bash
107	# 1. 從 Claude Code /status 取得 UUID，並指定 rendered alias。
108	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
109	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
110	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-agent-history-selectors.md'
111	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh \
112	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT"
113	
114	# 2. Stage code，再 stage 一組通過驗證的精確 transcript/plan。
115	git add path/to/feature.ts
116	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh \
117	  --session-only --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
118	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" --plan "$PLAN"
119	# 沒有 plan 時用 --no-plan。只有刻意沒有 rendered output 時，才把
120	# --no-specstory 與 --session-id 一起用；不會依 mtime 選 plan。
121	
122	# 3. 從 staged artifacts 產生 canonical final trailer block。
123	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
124	
125	# 4. 掃描 secret，再驗證完整英文 commit message。
126	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
127	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
128	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
129	
130	# 5. Commit。Pre-commit 會把 redact + gitleaks 當成 catch-all 再跑一次。
131	git commit -F /path/to/commit-message.txt
132	```
133	
134	Metadata helper 讀 staged blob，而不是仍可能被背景程序修改的 working file。
135	它輸出去重後的 `AI-Assisted-By: Harness (model)`、`Agent-Transcript` 與有 plan
136	時的 `Agent-Plan`。只有 transcript 無法證明 identity 時，才同時傳入
137	`--harness` 與 `--model`。
138	
139	`find-session.sh` 預設使用精確選擇。它以 git root 為錨點，驗證完整的 SpecStory
140	`Claude Code Session UUID` header，並解析指定的 Claude JSONL，要求 `sessionId`
141	與 `cwd` 完全相符。TSV 與 `--json` 都輸出 `status`、`confidence`、`source`、
142	選到的 path 與 ambiguity candidates。找不到 artifact、同一 UUID 有多個 alias，
143	或 identity 不符時都回傳 nonzero；只有明確的 `--newest` 才走 heuristic mode。
144	
145	`stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` 會先驗證所有 selector 與 path，最後只用
146	一次 `git add` 更新 index。Selector 失敗時 exit 5，index 保持不變。不帶 selector
147	的命令保留為**寬範圍 branch-wide compatibility mode**，會 stage 設定目錄內所有
148	髒的 Markdown；只有真的想包含整組檔案時才使用。

150	## SpecStory 2.10 的 checkout scope
151	
152	SpecStory 2.10 的實測行為：rendered output discovery 與 Claude raw session
153	discovery 都依 **checkout path，而不是 branch** 分隔。同一 checkout 切換 branch
154	仍共用 artifact pool；不同 worktree 才有不同的 `.specstory/history/` root 與
155	Claude project slug。
156	
157	採用 **先建 worktree，再啟動 wrapper/session** 的順序，每個 change stream 只跑
158	一組 SpecStory wrapper 與 Claude session。要明確 render 已知的 raw session：
159	
160	```bash
161	specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
162	```
163	
164	同一 UUID 可能產生多個 rendered alias。這是 ambiguity，不應用 newest-file
165	破除平手；請傳 `--specstory-path`。`EnterWorktree` 不會重新綁定已在運行的
166	SpecStory watcher，所以要先停止它，再從目標 worktree 啟動新的 wrapper。
167	
168	## SpecStory 原生 redaction（v2.4.0+）
169	
170	SpecStory 現在自己就會 redact secret，所以這個 skill 對
171	`.specstory/history/` 已經不是第一道防線了。
172	
173	| 出處 | 內容 |
174	|---|---|
175	| [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) | `feat(redaction): automatically redact secrets from saved markdown history` —— 社群貢獻者 [@warnes](https://github.com/warnes) 提出，2026-07-20 merged |
176	| [PR #253](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/253) | #235 的 `gofmt` CI 修正分支；最後 close 掉走 #235 |
177	| **v2.4.0**（2026-07-20） | 正式釋出，**預設開啟**，改用 [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset，且涵蓋本地 markdown **與** cloud sync |
178	| [#274](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/274)（open） | 相關的另一個洩漏面向 —— `specstory watch` 把 cloud auth token 放進 process command line |
179	
180	實際 merge 的程式碼跟 PR 不同：維護者把 PR 裡 11 條 inline regex 換成
181	Betterleaks，而 PR 的 `extra_patterns`（自訂 regex）沒有在這次改寫中存活。
182	`.specstory/cli/config.toml` 的 `[redaction] enabled`（或 `--no-redact-secrets`）
183	是唯一的開關。
184	
185	### 實測覆蓋率
186	
187	`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py` 會合成一個 Claude Code session，
188	用 `specstory sync --print` 跑兩次（有 / 無 `--no-redact-secrets`），
189	再逐個 secret class 比對。對 specstory 2.9.0、共 54 組 class/context：
190	
191	| 由誰攔下 | 組數 | 例子 |
192	|---|---:|---|
193	| SpecStory | 36 | Anthropic、OpenAI、GitHub PAT/OAuth/Actions、GitLab、Google、Groq、Slack、Stripe、Supabase、Linear、PEM block、`.env` dump |
194	| **只有我們** | 15 | Cursor、Tailscale、Discord/Zapier/Make webhook —— 以及 HuggingFace、Notion、WakaTime、OpenAI project key 出現在**散文**中時 |
195	| 都沒攔到 | 3 | `AKIA…` access key ID；散文中的 Telegram bot token |
196	
197	結構性發現：Betterleaks 有好幾類只在 `KEY=value` 形式下、透過基於 entropy 的
198	`generic-api-key` rule 才攔得到。同一個 token 出現在句子裡 —— 而這正是工具
199	transcript 實際印出 token 的方式 —— 就會直接漏過去。我們以 prefix 錨定的
200	rule 不在乎前後語法。
201	
202	### 兩層如何避免互相打架
203	
204	兩邊都寫同一個 sentinel：`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`（SpecStory 的 binary 帶有
205	格式字串 `[REDACTED:%s]`），而 `.gitleaks.toml` 把這個形狀加進 allowlist。
206	SpecStory 已經清理過的 transcript 會原封不動通過 hook —— 不會出現
207	「files were modified by this hook」，不用重新 `git add`，也不用再 commit 一次。
208	
209	redactor 改寫成 `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`，不再寫 `sk-abc...xyz` 截斷形式；
210	PEM block 則變成 `[REDACTED:private-key]` —— 正好就是 SpecStory 用的標籤。
211	截斷形式仍保留在 console 報告中，那裡的指紋有助於判斷該去 rotate 哪把 key。
212	`--legacy` 會改回 2.4.0 之前的 placeholder，它只改變寫入的位元組，
213	不影響偵測到什麼。
214	
215	（另一條相關規則 —— 散文中單純提到 `PRIVATE KEY` 不算金鑰材料，
216	`detect-private-key` 找的是 `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` 標頭 —— 由 redactor
217	以標頭為範圍的比對獨立保證。）
218	
219	## 洩漏後的紀律 (Post-leak discipline)
220	
221	`scan-staged.sh` 的 exit code 依洩漏狀態分支 (0 clean、10 redacted、
222	20 leaks、30 沒裝 gitleaks)。當有洩漏溜過去：
223	
224	1. **在供應商端輪換 (rotate)。** 這是唯一真正撤銷 credential 的動作。
225	   連結見 `references/remediation.md` §1。
226	2. **評估爆炸半徑 (blast radius)。** 本地未 push？feature branch？main？
227	3. **只在便宜時才清洗 (scrub)。** 未 push commit 用 amend 或
228	   `reset --soft`；feature branch 用 `git filter-repo` +
229	   force-with-lease；**永遠不要**改寫 `main`。
230	
231	runbook 顯式禁止對共用 branch 做 `git push --force` —— 詳見
232	`references/remediation.md` §5。
233	
234	## Gotchas
235	
236	- Branch 名稱不會限制 SpecStory 2.10 或 Claude raw-session discovery；checkout
237	  path 才會。不要用 `--newest` 推測某次 commit 的精確 session。
238	- 設定 `core.hooksPath` 後，`.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` 不會執行。
239	  `bootstrap-project.sh --install-hook` 現在會 exit 6，而不是安裝一個無效 hook。
240	- Claude/Cursor 原生 attribution 可以保留。可攜 minimum 是最後的
241	  `AI-Assisted-By` + transcript/plan block；不要虛構 AI email，也不要把 message
242	  attribution 說成 cryptographic signing。
243	
244	- SpecStory ≥ 2.4.0 寫檔時就已經 redact —— 別讓 hook 再做一次，
245	  見上面的「SpecStory 原生 redaction」。
246	- Claude Code 的 project-level `plansDirectory` 有時會被忽略
247	  ([issue #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537))；
248	  把它設在 user-level (`~/.claude/settings.json`) 當預設。
249	- `gitleaks protect` 從 v8.19.0 起被棄用 —— 用 `gitleaks git --staged`。
250	  skill 中所有地方都用現代語法。
251	- `pre-commit install` 是 per-clone —— 每個隊友（跟 CI）都必須跑，
252	  hook 才會觸發。
253	- 全域 `core.hooksPath` 只在 repo 有 `.pre-commit-config.yaml` 時才執行；
254	  bootstrap 之前的裸 repo 是不受保護的。

17	## Layout
18	
19	- `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.

25	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
26	  redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
27	  `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
28	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
29	  in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
30	  the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
31	  not on `PATH`.
32	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
33	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing

35	- `test_find_session.sh` — exact `sessionId`/`cwd` and SpecStory-header matching,
36	  explicit `--newest`, same-checkout branch leakage, duplicate UUID candidates,
37	  root-relative paths with spaces, subdirectory calls, and two-worktree isolation.
38	- `test_stage_agent_artifacts.sh` — exact plan/no-plan/no-SpecStory policy, one
39	  atomic `git add`, unchanged-index selector failures, broad-mode compatibility,
40	  exact metadata trailers, and generated hook no-op/error/success behavior.
41	- `test_agent_commit_metadata.sh` — staged transcript parsing, model
42	  deduplication, spaced paths, JSON output, overrides, and bootstrap's global
43	  `core.hooksPath` refusal.
44	- `test_bootstrap_project.py` — verifies precise, idempotent nested SpecStory
45	  ignores; confirms `history/` stays visible; checks dry-run and the explicit
46	  `--untrack-specstory-state` migration contract.

48	## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
49	
50	The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
51	`webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
52	secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
53	`npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:
54	
55	```
56	<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->                      # markdown fixtures
57	"-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n"  # gitleaks:allow  # test_redact_secrets.py
58	```
59	
60	The Stripe webhook fixture is stricter: GitHub's provider-level scanner does
61	not honour gitleaks markers, so its source uses
62	`__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__`. The corpus test expands that placeholder
63	inside its throwaway repo. The other corpus + shell tests **strip the marker
64	before staging** (`_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE` in `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`; the `sed`
65	in `stage_fixture` in `test_scan_staged.sh`), so the secret bytes have the exact
66	shape the rules expect and the assertions still fire. Principle: **fake test
67	vectors are out of scan scope by default, and only "fire" when a test re-plants
68	them.**
69	
70	Invariant — **the strip must be byte-identical**: never change a secret's length
71	or the length-sensitive rules (`sk-proj-…{80,}`, `sk-ant-api\d{2}-…{93}AA`, the
72	webhook regexes) stop matching. When adding a new firing fixture, append the
73	marker with a single leading space (`<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->`); the
74	strip regex reclaims exactly that separator. `clean.md` / `example_shapes.md`
75	carry no marker (the strip is a no-op) and must keep their must-not-fire
76	behavior. GitHub-native secret scanning ignores the marker; it's excluded
77	separately via the repo's `.github/secret_scanning.yml`. This replaced a former

89	| `gitleaks dir` silently skipped hidden paths                | `test_redact_secrets`    |
90	| JSON report `[]` treated as "leaks found"                   | `test_scan_staged.sh`    |

92	## Requirements

94	- `uv` (for `uv run --extra dev pytest`)
95	- `gitleaks` on `PATH` (corpus tests + shell test skip gracefully when
96	  missing — the pytest file xfails with a clear message, the shell
97	  test exits 0 for the "no gitleaks" case)
98	- `git` configured with a user identity (the shell test uses

 ## Layout
 
 - `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
   Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
   should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged

   `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
 - `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
   redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
   `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
 - `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
   in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
   the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
   not on `PATH`.
 - `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for

   gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.

+  explicit `--newest`, same-checkout branch leakage, duplicate UUID candidates,

+  exact metadata trailers, and generated hook no-op/error/success behavior.

 ## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
 
 The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
 `webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
 secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
 `npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:

```text
1	# Transcript & session discovery
2	
3	How `find-session.sh` proves that one SpecStory Markdown file and one Claude Code
4	JSONL belong to the same session in the current git checkout.
5	
6	## Exact by default
7	
8	There is no reliable implicit "current session" pointer. Multiple sessions can
9	write under one checkout, and branch switches do not move those files. Therefore
10	`find-session.sh` requires at least one exact selector:
11	
12	```bash
13	# UUID from Claude Code /status
14	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
15	  --session-id 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
16	
17	# Explicit rendered alias; relative paths resolve from the git root
18	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
19	  --specstory-path '.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
20	
21	# Strongest form: both selectors must agree
22	bash scripts/find-session.sh \
23	  --session-id 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab \
24	  --specstory-path '.specstory/history/2026-08-28_08-00-00Z.md'
25	```
26	
27	`--newest` is an explicit compatibility heuristic. It independently picks the
28	newest SpecStory Markdown and Claude JSONL by mtime and reports
29	`confidence=heuristic`; it does not prove that the two files belong together.
30	Never use it for exact staging or hooks.
31	
32	## Git-root anchoring
33	
34	The script starts with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and anchors all discovery
35	to that path. Calling it from `src/deep/subdir` is therefore equivalent to
36	calling it from the checkout root. A relative `--specstory-path` is also
37	interpreted from the git root, not the shell's current subdirectory.
38	
39	Paths must be regular Markdown files directly under the checkout's
40	`.specstory/history/`. Outside paths and malformed headers fail closed.
41	
42	## Claude Code session layout and proof
43	
44	Claude Code stores raw sessions under:
45	
46	```
47	~/.claude/projects/<checkout-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl
48	```
49	
50	The slug is the absolute git-root path with **every non-alphanumeric character**
51	replaced by `-`, including dots, underscores, and spaces. For example,
52	`/home/user/.local/project one` becomes
53	`-home-user--local-project-one`. Rebuild it with
54	`sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'`, not `tr '/' '-'`.
55	
56	Exact resolution does not trust the filename alone. It parses complete JSONL
57	records and requires one object whose:
58	
59	- `sessionId` exactly equals the selected UUID; and
60	- `cwd` exactly equals the current git root.
61	
62	A live writer may leave one incomplete trailing JSON line; malformed lines are
63	ignored, but another complete record still has to prove both fields. A correctly
64	named file with another checkout's `cwd` exits as a mismatch.
65	
66	## SpecStory layout, header, and aliases
67	
68	SpecStory writes rendered output under:
69	
70	```
71	<git-root>/.specstory/history/<rendered-name>.md
72	```
73	
74	For Claude sessions, exact matching requires this whole header shape:
75	
76	```markdown
77	<!-- Claude Code Session 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab (2026-08-28 08:00:00Z) -->
78	```
79	
80	`--session-id` scans header UUIDs, not filenames or substring matches. One UUID
81	can have multiple rendered aliases. In that case the script returns
82	`status=ambiguous`, lists every candidate, exits 4, and requires an explicit
83	`--specstory-path` to disambiguate. When both selectors are supplied, the path's
84	header UUID must exactly equal `--session-id`.
85	
86	To render one known raw session explicitly with SpecStory 2.10:
87	
88	```bash
89	specstory sync claude -s 01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
90	```
91	
92	If that creates another alias for a UUID already present, select the intended
93	path explicitly; do not infer from its timestamp.
94	
95	## SpecStory 2.10 scoping: checkout path, not branch
96	
97	Verified behavior in SpecStory 2.10:
98	
99	- Rendered output discovery is scoped to the checkout path containing
100	  `.specstory/history/`, not to the checked-out branch name.
101	- Raw Claude session discovery is likewise scoped through the checkout path's
102	  Claude project slug, not its branch.
103	- Switching branches in one checkout therefore exposes the same session pool.
104	  Newest-file selection can pick a transcript produced on another branch.
105	- Two worktrees have different roots, SpecStory history directories, and Claude
106	  project slugs. Prefer **worktree first, wrapper/session second**.
107	- Run one SpecStory wrapper/session per change stream. If a stream moves, stop
108	  the old wrapper and start a new one in the target worktree.
109	- `EnterWorktree` changes the agent's working directory; it does **not** rebind a
110	  SpecStory watcher that was already running against another checkout.
111	
112	This is why branch identity never appears in the exact selector contract. The
113	stable tuple is checkout root + session UUID + rendered path when needed.
114	
115	## Structured output
116	
117	TSV is the default and always starts with resolution metadata:
118	
119	```text
120	status	resolved
121	confidence	exact
122	source	session-id+specstory-path
123	specstory_path	/absolute/checkout/.specstory/history/session.md
124	claude_session_uuid	01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
125	claude_jsonl_path	/absolute/home/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl
126	```
127	
128	Ambiguous or invalid selections add repeated `candidate<TAB>path` rows. `--json`
129	emits the same fields plus a `candidates` array as one JSON object. Diagnostics
130	go to stderr; `--quiet` suppresses those diagnostics without hiding structured
131	stdout.
132	
133	| Exit | Meaning |
134	|---:|---|
135	| 0 | Requested exact artifacts resolved, or explicit heuristic succeeded |
136	| 1 | Invalid/missing arguments |
137	| 2 | Not inside a git repository |
138	| 3 | Requested artifact not found |
139	| 4 | Exact UUID has multiple rendered candidates |
140	| 5 | Path, header, or JSONL identity mismatch |
141	
142	These nonzero exits are intentional. Callers must not convert absence or
143	ambiguity into an empty "success" and then guess.
144	
145	## Exact staging handoff
146	
147	`stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` calls this resolver before touching
148	the index. It requires exact identity plus exactly one of `--plan PATH` or
149	`--no-plan`; use `--no-specstory` only with `--session-id` when rendered output
150	is intentionally absent. Resolver failures map to staging exit 5 and leave the
151	index unchanged.
152	
153	The staging script's no-selector invocation remains broad branch-wide
154	compatibility mode. It stages all dirty Markdown under configured artifact
155	directories and does not claim session identity.
156	
157	## Cross-reference
158	
159	- [`pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](./pre-commit-redaction-stack.md) — how
160	  selected files are scanned and redacted at commit time.
161	- [`../scripts/find-session.sh`](../scripts/find-session.sh) — exact resolver.
162	- [`../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh`](../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh) —
163	  validation and one-shot index update.
164
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# find-session.sh — resolve the current agent session files for $PWD.
#
# Returns the SpecStory transcript path + Claude Code session UUID/JSONL
# path for the current working directory, so the calling agent can stage
# the right artifacts before a commit.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: find-session.sh [OPTIONS]

Discover the agent session files associated with $PWD. Heuristics:
  - SpecStory: newest *.md under ./.specstory/history/
  - Claude Code: newest *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ where
                 <slug> is $PWD with '/' -> '-' (Claude's own convention).

Options:
  --format=VALUE     one of: specstory, claude, both (default: both)
  --json             Emit JSON instead of TSV.
  --quiet            Suppress stderr diagnostics on empty results.
  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.

Output (TSV, one key/value per line):
  specstory_path       <abs path or empty>
  claude_session_uuid  <uuid or empty>
  claude_jsonl_path    <abs path or empty>

Exit codes:
  0  always (never fails the pipeline; empty values signal absence).
  1  invalid arguments.
EOF
}

log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

FORMAT="both"
OUT_JSON=0
QUIET=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
    --format)   FORMAT="${2:-both}"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)     OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
    --quiet)    QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)         die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)          die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
  esac
done

case "$FORMAT" in
  both|specstory|claude) ;;
  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
esac

# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with every NON-ALPHANUMERIC character
# replaced by '-' -- not just '/'.
#   /Volumes/Data/x          -> -Volumes-Data-x
#   /home/u/.local/share/foo -> -home-u--local-share-foo   (the dot collapses)
# The leading dash is intentional -- it mirrors how Claude Code names the
# subdirectory under ~/.claude/projects/. Using `tr '/' '-'` here silently
# returns an empty result for any path containing '.', '_' or a space.
cwd_slug() {
  printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9]|-|g'
}

newest_file() {
  # newest_file <dir> <glob>
  # Prints the newest matching file by mtime, or empty if none.
  local dir="$1" glob="$2"
  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
  # stat -f on macOS, stat -c on Linux — use find+sort for portability.
  local found
  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
    | head -n 1)
  printf '%s' "$found"
}

SPECSTORY_PATH=""
CLAUDE_JSONL=""
CLAUDE_UUID=""

if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
  candidate=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
    SPECSTORY_PATH="$candidate"
  else
    log "no .specstory/history/*.md under $PWD"
  fi
fi

if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
  slug=$(cwd_slug)
  proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$slug"
  candidate=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
    CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
    CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$candidate" .jsonl)
  else
    log "no ~/.claude/projects/$slug/*.jsonl (slug derived from PWD)"
  fi
fi

if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
  # Hand-rolled JSON keeps us dependency-free (no jq/python requirement).
  printf '{"specstory_path":"%s","claude_session_uuid":"%s","claude_jsonl_path":"%s"}\n' \
    "$SPECSTORY_PATH" "$CLAUDE_UUID" "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
else
  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
  printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
  printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
fi
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
# the next commit.
#
# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]

Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.

Options:
  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.

Exit codes:
  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
  1  invalid arguments
  2  not inside a git repo
  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

SESSION_ONLY=0
INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
DRY_RUN=0
ALLOW_EMPTY=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Must be in a git repo.
if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "not inside a git repo" 2
fi
REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
fi

ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  # Strip comments and whitespace.
  line="${line%%#*}"
  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
done < "$DIRS_FILE"

# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
check_ignored() {
  local dir="$1"
  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
  fi
}

# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
find_current_specstory() {
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
}
find_current_plan() {
  [ -d ".claude/plans" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
  find .claude/plans -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null \
    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
list_dirty_artifacts() {
  local dir path git_status
  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
    check_ignored "$dir"
    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
      # We only want the path portion.
      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
      path="${entry:3}"
      case "$path" in
        *.md) ;;
        *) continue ;;
      esac
      case "$git_status" in
        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
        "M "|"A ")
          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
          ;;
      esac
    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
  done
}

# --- Main ---
STAGED_COUNT=0
CANDIDATES=()

if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
  plan=$(find_current_plan)
  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
else
  # Capture the dirty artifact list.
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    CANDIDATES+=("$f")
  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
fi

# Check: are there code changes outside the artifact dirs?
# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
has_code_changes() {
  local any=0 line path in_artifact dir
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
    path="${line:3}"
    in_artifact=0
    for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
      case "$path" in
        "$dir"/*) in_artifact=1; break ;;
      esac
    done
    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$any" = "1" ]
}

if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  if has_code_changes; then
    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
    exit 0
  fi
  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
  exit 3
fi

if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
  exit 4
fi

# Stage (or print).
for f in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$f"
  else
    git add -- "$f"
    printf 'staged: %s\n' "$f"
  fi
  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))
done

log "${STAGED_COUNT} artifact(s) ${DRY_RUN:+would be }staged."
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban

65	```
66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	Active series in this repo:
76	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
77	
78	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
79	
80	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
81	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
82	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
83	
84	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
85	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
86	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
87	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
88	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
89	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
90	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
91	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
92	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
93	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
94	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
95	
96	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
97	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
98	
99	## Marketplace Catalog
100	
101	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
102	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
103	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
104	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
105	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
106	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
107	for the full mechanism.
108	
109	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
110	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
111	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
112	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
113	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
114	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
115	
116	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
117	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
118	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
119	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
120	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
121	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
122	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
123	within-group caveat in
124	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
125	
126	## SKILL.md Format
127	
128	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
129	
130	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
131	
132	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
133	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
134	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
135	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
136	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
137	
138	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
139	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
140	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
141	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
142	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
143	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
144	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
145	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
146	
147	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
148	
149	```bash
150	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
151	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
152	
153	# …or remove them afterward
154	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
155	```
156	
157	## Project Memory Workflow
158	
159	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
160	
161	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
162	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
163	
164	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
165	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
166	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
167	
168	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
169	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
170	
171	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
172	
173	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
174	
175	   ```bash
176	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
177	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
178	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
179	   ```
180	
181	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
182	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
183	
184	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
185	
186	   ```bash
187	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
191	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
192	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
193	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
194	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
195	
196	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
197	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
198	   afterwards to catch drift.
199	
200	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
201	
202	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
203	
204	```bash
205	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
206	```
207	
208	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
209	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
210	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
211	
212	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
213	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
214	
215	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
216	
217	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
218	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
219	own conventions). It has three subareas:
220	
221	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
222	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
223	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
224	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
225	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
226	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
227	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
228	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
229	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
230	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
231	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
232	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
233	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
234	  status / license / last_verified`).
235	
236	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
237	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
238	
239	| Status | Meaning |
240	|---|---|
241	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
242	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
243	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
244	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
245	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
246	
247	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
248	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
249	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
250	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
251	
252	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
253	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
254	
255	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
256	
257	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
258	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
259	
260	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
261	2. The root cause
262	3. The workaround
263	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
264	
265	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
266	the explanation they do not know yet.
267
```

11	
12	Resolve agent session files for the current git checkout. Exact selectors are
13	required unless the caller explicitly opts into the compatibility heuristic.
14	Relative paths are resolved from the git root, not the invocation directory.
15	
16	Selectors:
17	  --session-id UUID       Select an exact canonical lowercase Claude Code UUID.
18	                          When SpecStory output is requested, its header must match.
19	  --specstory-path PATH   Select one exact direct-child
20	                          .specstory/history/*.md file and derive/verify its UUID.
21	  --newest                Explicitly use independent newest-file heuristics.
22	                          Cannot be combined with exact selectors.

25	  --format VALUE          specstory, claude, or both (default: both).
26	  --json                  Emit one JSON object instead of TSV.
27	  --quiet                 Suppress stderr diagnostics; structured stdout remains.
28	  --help, -h              Show this help and exit.
29	
30	TSV output keys:
31	  status                  resolved | not_found | ambiguous | mismatch | error
32	  confidence              exact | heuristic | none
33	  source                  session-id | specstory-path | session-id+specstory-path | newest
34	  specstory_path          absolute path or empty
35	  claude_session_uuid     canonical lowercase UUID or empty
36	  claude_jsonl_path       absolute path or empty
37	  candidate               repeated absolute candidate path (only when relevant)

40	  0  requested artifacts resolved
41	  1  invalid arguments
42	  2  not inside a git repository
43	  3  requested artifact not found
44	  4  exact selector is ambiguous; candidates are reported

211	    /*) absolute="$input" ;;
212	    *)  absolute="$REPO_ROOT/$input" ;;
213	  esac

215	  [ -f "$absolute" ] || return 1

230	# Read exactly the fixed two-line SpecStory preamble. Large transcript bodies

232	specstory_header_uuid() {
233	  local path="$1" generated="" marker="" marker_re
234	  exec 3< "$path" || return 1
235	  IFS= read -r generated <&3 || { exec 3<&-; return 1; }
236	  IFS= read -r marker <&3 || { exec 3<&-; return 1; }
237	  exec 3<&-
238	  [ "$generated" = '<!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 -->' ] || return 1
239	  marker_re='^<!-- Claude Code Session ([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}) \([^)]*\) -->$'
240	  [[ "$marker" =~ $marker_re ]] || return 1
241	  printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
242	}

244	validate_specstory_path() {

247	  [ "$root_rc" = "0" ] || return 2
248	  [ ! -L "$path" ] || return 2
249	  [ -f "$path" ] || return 1

251	  [ "$parent" = "$SPECSTORY_DIR" ] || return 2
252	  case "$(basename "$path")" in *.md) ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
253	  uuid="$(specstory_header_uuid "$path")" || return 3
254	  [ -n "$uuid" ] || return 3

258	validate_claude_jsonl() {
259	  local path="$1" uuid="$2"

261	  python3 - "$path" "$uuid" "$REPO_ROOT" <<'PY'

263	import os
264	import subprocess
265	import sys
266	
267	path, expected_session, expected_root = sys.argv[1:]
268	expected_root = os.path.realpath(expected_root)
269	matched = False
270	root_cache = {}
271	
272	
273	def git_root(cwd):
274	    if not isinstance(cwd, str) or not cwd:
275	        return None
276	    if cwd in root_cache:
277	        return root_cache[cwd]
278	    try:
279	        result = subprocess.run(
280	            ["git", "-C", cwd, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
281	            check=True,
282	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
283	            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
284	            text=True,
285	        )
286	        value = os.path.realpath(result.stdout.rstrip("\n"))
287	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
288	        value = None
289	    root_cache[cwd] = value
290	    return value
291	
292	
293	def incomplete_json(text, error):
294	    stripped = text.rstrip()
295	    return error.msg.startswith("Unterminated") or error.pos >= max(0, len(stripped) - 1)
296	
297	
298	try:
299	    with open(path, "rb") as stream:
300	        for raw in stream:
301	            terminated = raw.endswith(b"\n")
302	            try:
303	                text = raw.decode("utf-8")
304	            except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
305	                if not terminated and error.end == len(raw):
306	                    continue
307	                sys.exit(2)
308	            try:
309	                value = json.loads(text)
310	            except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
311	                if not terminated and incomplete_json(text, error):
312	                    continue
313	                sys.exit(2)
314	            if not isinstance(value, dict):
315	                sys.exit(2)
316	            if value.get("sessionId") == expected_session:
317	                if git_root(value.get("cwd")) == expected_root:
318	                    matched = True
319	except (OSError, UnicodeError):
320	    sys.exit(2)
321	
322	sys.exit(0 if matched else 1)
323	PY
324	}

326	newest_file() {
327	  local dir="$1" glob="$2" newest="" file
328	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
329	  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
330	    if [ -z "$newest" ] || [ "$file" -nt "$newest" ]; then newest="$file"; fi
331	  done < <(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null)

292	# Complete path validation before any index mutation.
293	for artifact in "${CANDIDATES[@]:-}"; do
294	  [ -n "$artifact" ] || continue
295	  validate_candidate_path "$artifact"

298	if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
299	  if has_code_changes; then

301	    exit 0
302	  fi
303	  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."

307	if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
308	  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes are present."
309	  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
310	  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if this artifact-only change is intentional."

312	fi

314	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then

317	  done
318	  log "${#CANDIDATES[@]} artifact(s) validated; index unchanged."
319	  exit 0

322	# One git process updates the index only after every selector/path check passed.
323	git add -- "${CANDIDATES[@]}"

325	  printf 'staged: %s\n' "$artifact"
326	done
327	log "${#CANDIDATES[@]} artifact(s) staged atomically."

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

Two standing rules: every run that exercises the model spends real money, so get the user's approval first; and when context for a lever is missing, work through it interactively with the user - this workflow is not expected to one-shot the audit. Do not summarize the guide - execute it; presenting the profile and the ranked plan to the user is part of executing it. |
